title.zh: 卷七十二 列傳第六十二 文學
title.raw: 卷七十二 列傳第六十二 文學 Volume 72 Biographies 62: Men of Letters

sentences.zh: 丘靈鞠檀超卞彬丘巨源王智深崔慰祖祖沖之賈希鏡袁峻劉昭鍾嶸周興嗣吳均劉勰何思澄任孝恭顏協紀少瑜杜之偉顏晃岑之敬何之元徐伯陽張正見阮卓

translations.literal: Qiu Lingju, Tan Chao, Bian Bin, Qiu Juyuan, Wang Zhishen, Cui Weizu, Zu Chongzhi, Jia Xijing, Yuan Jun, Liu Zhao, Zhong Rong, Zhou Xingsi, Wu Jun, Liu Xie, He Sicheng, Ren Xiaogong, Yan Xie, Ji Shaoyu, Du Zhiwei, Yan Huang, Cen Zhijing, He Zhiyuan, Xu Boyang, Zhang Zhengjian, Ruan Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lingju, Tan Chao, Bian Bin, Qiu Juyuan, Wang Zhishen, Cui Weizu, Zu Chongzhi, Jia Xijing, Yuan Jun, Liu Zhao, Zhong Rong, Zhou Xingsi, Wu Jun, Liu Xie, He Sicheng, Ren Xiaogong, Yan Xie, Ji Shaoyu, Du Zhiwei, Yan Huang, Cen Zhijing, He Zhiyuan, Xu Boyang, Zhang Zhengjian, and Ruan Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 易云：「觀乎人文以化成天下。

translations.literal: The Yi says: "Observe the patterns of human culture to transform and perfect all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Contemplate the patterns of human culture to transform and civilize all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」孔子曰：「煥乎其有文章。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "How brilliant is its literary adornment!"
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "How splendidly it shines with literary grace!"

sentences.zh: 」自漢以來，辭人代有，大則憲章典誥，小則申抒性靈。

translations.literal: Since the Han, generations have had men of letters; on the grand scale they framed canonical pronouncements and edicts, on the small they gave voice to inner feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han dynasty, each age has produced writers of note: at the grand level they shaped canonical models and state documents; at the intimate level they gave expression to the inner life of the spirit.

sentences.zh: 至於經禮樂而緯國家，通古今而述美惡，非斯則莫可也。

translations.literal: As for threading ritual and music through the state and linking past and present to set forth good and evil, nothing else could accomplish this.
translations.idiomatic: When it comes to weaving ritual and music through the fabric of the state, or spanning past and present to record what is admirable and what is base, nothing else can do the work.

sentences.zh: 是以哲王在上，咸所敦悅。

translations.literal: Therefore sage kings on high have all cherished and delighted in it.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason enlightened rulers on the throne have all honored and delighted in literary culture.

sentences.zh: 故云：「言之不文，行之不遠」。

translations.literal: Hence it is said: "If words lack refinement, they will not travel far."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "Words without polish do not carry far."

sentences.zh: 自中原沸騰，五馬南度，綴文之士，無乏于時。

translations.literal: From the time the Central Plains seethed and the five imperial horses crossed south, men who polished prose were never lacking in that age.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the Central Plains boiled with turmoil and the five imperial scions fled south, men skilled at literary composition have never been wanting.

sentences.zh: 降及梁朝，其流彌盛。

translations.literal: By the time of the Liang dynasty, that current had grown all the fuller.
translations.idiomatic: By the Liang dynasty the literary current had swollen to its height.

sentences.zh: 蓋由時主儒雅，篤好文章，故才秀之士，煥乎俱集。

translations.literal: This was largely because the rulers of the age were refined and Confucian and deeply devoted to literature, so talented and outstanding men gathered together in splendor.
translations.idiomatic: This was chiefly because the rulers of the day were cultivated and Confucian-minded, passionately devoted to letters, so men of talent and brilliance assembled in radiant company.

sentences.zh: 于時武帝每所臨幸，輒命群臣賦詩，其文之善者賜以金帛。

translations.literal: At that time, wherever Emperor Wu went on tour, he would order the ministers to compose poetry; those whose writings were excellent he rewarded with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: In those days, wherever Emperor Wu traveled he would have his ministers compose poems on the spot, and those whose work was finest received gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 是以縉紳之士，咸知自勵。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentry all knew to spur themselves on.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the scholar-official class all understood the need to strive and improve themselves.

sentences.zh: 至有陳受命，運接亂離，雖加獎勵，而向時之風流息矣。

translations.literal: When Chen received the Mandate, the age met with turmoil and separation; though rewards were still given, the elegance of former times had ceased.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Chen received the Mandate, the fortune of the age had turned to chaos and dispersal; though encouragement was still offered, the literary brilliance of earlier days had faded away.

sentences.zh: 詩云：「人之雲亡，邦國殄悴。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "When worthy men depart, the state and its altars are brought to ruin."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs says: "When good men are gone, the state and its altars waste away."

sentences.zh: 」豈金陵之數將終三百年乎？

translations.literal: Could it be that Jinling's allotted span of three hundred years is nearing its end?
translations.idiomatic: Was the three-hundred-year destiny of Jinling now drawing to its close?

sentences.zh: 不然，何至是也。

translations.literal: If not, how could it have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how could things have reached such a pass?

sentences.zh: 宋史不立文學傳，齊、梁皆有其目。

translations.literal: The History of Song did not establish a "Men of Letters" section; both Qi and Liang had such a category.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Song did not include a biographical section for men of letters, but both the Qi and Liang histories did.

sentences.zh: 今綴而序之，以備此篇云爾。

translations.literal: Now I have gathered and arranged them in sequence to complete this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: I have now gathered and arranged their accounts in order to complete this chapter.

sentences.zh: 丘靈鞠，吳興烏程人也。

translations.literal: Qiu Lingju was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Lingju was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖系，秘書監。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xi was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xi served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父道真，護軍長史。

translations.literal: His father Daozhen was Chief Clerk to the Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daozhen served as Chief Clerk to the Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠少好學，善屬文，州辟從事。

translations.literal: Lingju from youth loved learning and was skilled at literary composition; the province recruited him as an Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Lingju loved learning from youth and excelled at literary composition; the province appointed him as an Attendant.

sentences.zh: 詣領軍沈演之，演之曰：「身昔為州職，詣領軍謝晦，賓主坐處，政如今日。

translations.literal: He called on the Commander-in-Chief Shen Yanzhi, who said: "I was once in a provincial post and called on the Commander-in-Chief Xie Hui; host and guest sat just as we do today."
translations.idiomatic: He called on Commander-in-Chief Shen Yanzhi, who said, "When I was once in a provincial post I called on Commander-in-Chief Xie Hui; host and guest sat exactly as we do today."

sentences.zh: 卿將來復如此也。

translations.literal: You too will come to this again in the future."
translations.idiomatic: You too will find yourself in this same situation again someday."

sentences.zh: 」累遷員外郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Outer Gentleman Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Outer Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，為通直常侍，尋領東觀祭酒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and soon served concurrently as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Lingju was appointed Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and soon became Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion as well.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠曰：「人居官願數遷，使我終身為祭酒不恨也。

translations.literal: Lingju said: "When a man holds office he wishes for frequent promotions; yet if I could spend my whole life as Libationer I would have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Lingju said, "Men in office usually long for frequent promotion, yet if I could remain Libationer for life I would feel no regret."

sentences.zh: 」永明二年，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he served concurrently as General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming he was appointed concurrent General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠不樂武位，謂人曰：「我應還東掘顧榮塚。

translations.literal: Lingju took no pleasure in a military post and told others: "I ought to go back east and dig up Gu Rong's tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Lingju took no joy in a military appointment and said to others, "I ought to go back east and dig up Gu Rong's grave."

sentences.zh: 江南地方數千里，士子風流皆出此中。

translations.literal: The lands south of the Yangtze stretch for thousands of li, and the refinement of scholar-gentlemen all issued from this region.
translations.idiomatic: The lands south of the Yangtze stretch for thousands of li, and the cultivated brilliance of the gentry all sprang from this country.

sentences.zh: 顧榮忽引諸傖輩度，妨我輩塗轍，死有餘罪。」

translations.literal: Yet Gu Rong suddenly led all those coarse northerners across, blocking our path—he deserved death and more."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gu Rong suddenly led all those coarse outsiders across the river, blocking our path—death would still have been too light a punishment for him."

sentences.zh: 靈鞠好飲酒，臧否人物，在沈深座，見王儉詩，深曰：「王令文章大進。

translations.literal: Lingju loved wine and passed judgment on people. At Shen Shen's table he saw Wang Jian's poetry; Shen said: "Master Wang's writing has made great progress."
translations.idiomatic: Lingju loved wine and was quick to praise or condemn others. At Shen Shen's gathering he saw Wang Jian's poems; Shen said, "Master Wang's writing has improved enormously."

sentences.zh: 」靈鞠曰：「何如我未進時。

translations.literal: Lingju said: "How does it compare with before he had made progress?"
translations.idiomatic: Lingju said, "How does it compare with before he improved?"

sentences.zh: 」此言達儉。

translations.literal: This remark reached Jian.
translations.idiomatic: This remark reached Wang Jian's ears.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠宋時文名甚盛，入齊頗減，蓬發弛縱無形儀，不事家業。

translations.literal: Under Song his literary fame had been very great; entering Qi it declined somewhat. With disheveled hair and unrestrained conduct he had no sense of decorum and did not attend to family affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song his literary reputation had been immense; in Qi it waned somewhat. With unkempt hair and unrestrained ways he cared nothing for propriety and neglected his household affairs.

sentences.zh: 王儉謂人曰：「丘公仕宦不進，才亦退矣。

translations.literal: Wang Jian said to others: "Master Qiu has not advanced in office, and his talent has retreated as well."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian remarked to others, "Master Qiu has not risen in office, and his talent has declined with it."

sentences.zh: 」位長沙王車騎長史，卒。

translations.literal: He held the post of Chief Clerk to the Chariots and Cavalry of the Prince of Changsha and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Chief Clerk to the Chariots and Cavalry of the Prince of Changsha, then died.

sentences.zh: 著江左文章錄序，起太興，訖元熙。

translations.literal: He wrote a preface to the Record of Writings of the Eastern Quarter, spanning from Taixing to Yuanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a preface to the Record of Writings of the Eastern Quarter, covering the period from Taixing through Yuanxi.

sentences.zh: 文集行于時。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 子遲。

translations.literal: His son was Chi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chi.

sentences.zh: 遲字希範，八歲便屬文。

translations.literal: Chi, styled Xifan, could compose prose at the age of eight.
translations.idiomatic: Chi, styled Xifan, was already composing literary pieces at the age of eight.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠常謂「氣骨似我」。

translations.literal: Lingju often said, "His spirit and bone-structure are like mine."
translations.idiomatic: Lingju often said of him, "His vital spirit and backbone are just like mine."

sentences.zh: 黃門郎謝超宗、征士何點並見而異之。

translations.literal: Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Xie Chaozong and Recluse He Dian both saw him and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Xie Chaozong and the recluse He Dian both met him and marveled at his gifts.

sentences.zh: 在齊，以秀才累遷殿中郎。

translations.literal: Under Qi, as a Cultivated Talent he was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he entered service as a Cultivated Talent and rose through successive promotions to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝平建鄴，引為驃騎主簿，甚被禮遇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jiankang, he summoned Chi as Chief Clerk to the Rapid Cavalry and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang pacified Jiankang, he appointed Chi Chief Clerk to the Rapid Cavalry and honored him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 時勸進梁王及殊禮，皆遲文也。

translations.literal: At that time the documents urging the Prince of Liang to advance and granting him special honors were all written by Chi.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials urging the Prince of Liang to take the throne and the edicts granting him extraordinary honors were all Chi's compositions.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，遷中書郎，待詔文德殿。

translations.literal: When the throne was taken, he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and awaited imperial commands in the Hall of Civil Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne, Chi was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and served as a drafting attendant in the Hall of Civil Virtue.

sentences.zh: 時帝著連珠，詔群臣繼作者數十人，遲文最美。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor composed linked pearls and ordered several dozen ministers to continue them; Chi's writing was the finest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had composed a linked-pearl poem and ordered several dozen ministers to write continuations; Chi's piece was judged the finest.

sentences.zh: 坐事免，乃獻責躬詩，上優辭答之。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense, then presented a poem of self-reproach; the emperor replied with gracious words.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed on a charge, he submitted a poem of self-reproach; the emperor answered with generous and gracious words.

sentences.zh: 後出為永嘉太守，在郡不稱職，為有司所糾。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Administrator of Yongjia; in the commandery he did not perform his duties well and was impeached by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was sent out as Administrator of Yongjia, where he failed to perform his duties adequately and was impeached by the supervising offices.

sentences.zh: 帝愛其才，寢其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor cherished his talent and set aside the memorial of impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his talent and suppressed the impeachment memorial.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，中軍將軍臨川王宏北侵魏，以為諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian, when Central Army General the Prince of Linchuan, Hong, invaded Wei in the north, Chi was made Advisory Army Major and served concurrently as Master of Records.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianjian, when Central Army General the Prince of Linchuan led a northern campaign against Wei, Chi was appointed Advisory Army Major and served concurrently as Master of Records.

sentences.zh: 時陳伯之在北，與魏軍來拒，遲以書喻之，伯之遂降。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Bozhi was in the north and came with Wei forces to resist; Chi sent him a letter of persuasion, and Bozhi thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Bozhi was then in the north fighting alongside Wei forces; Chi wrote him a letter of persuasion, and Bozhi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 還拜中書侍郎，遷司空從事中郎，卒官。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Minister of Works, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Minister of Works, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 遲辭采麗逸，時有鍾嶸著詩評云：「範雲婉轉清便，如流風回雪。

translations.literal: Chi's literary style was beautiful and graceful. At the time Zhong Rong wrote in his Critique of Poetry: "Fan Yun is supple and clear, like wind in flow and snow whirling back."
translations.idiomatic: Chi's style was lush and graceful. Zhong Rong wrote in his Critique of Poetry: "Fan Yun is supple and lucid, like wind streaming and snow swirling back."

sentences.zh: 遲點綴映媚，似落花依草。

translations.literal: Chi adorns and gleams with charm, like fallen blossoms resting on grass."
translations.idiomatic: Chi adorns his lines with charm, like fallen blossoms resting against the grass."

sentences.zh: 雖取賤文通，而秀於敬子。

translations.literal: Though he ranks below Wen Tong, he surpasses Jingzi."
translations.idiomatic: Though he ranks below Wen Tong, he outshines Jingzi."

sentences.zh: 」其見稱如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he praised.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the praise he received.

sentences.zh: 仲孚字公信，靈鞠從孫也。

translations.literal: Zhongfu, styled Gongxin, was Lingju's grandnephew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu, styled Gongxin, was a grandnephew of Lingju.

sentences.zh: 少好學，讀書常以中宵鍾鳴為限。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and often took the midnight bell as his limit for reading.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and often read until the midnight bell sounded.

sentences.zh: 靈鞠嘗稱為千里駒也。

translations.literal: Lingju once called him a steed of a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Lingju once called him a colt that would run a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 齊永明初，為國子生。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming under Qi he was a student of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongming under Qi he enrolled as a student of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 王儉曰：「東南之美，復見丘生。

translations.literal: Wang Jian said: "The finest of the southeast—I see a Qiu again."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian said, "The finest talent of the southeast—we have another Qiu among us."

sentences.zh: 」舉高第，未調，還鄉里。

translations.literal: He passed the examination with highest honors but received no appointment and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination with highest honors but received no appointment and returned home.

sentences.zh: 家貧，乃結群盜為之計，劫掠三吳。

translations.literal: His family was poor, so he joined with bandits in a plan and plundered the Three Wu region.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, so he joined a band of robbers and raided throughout the Three Wu region.

sentences.zh: 仲孚聰明有智略，群盜畏服，所行皆果，故亦不發。

translations.literal: Zhongfu was clever and resourceful; the bandits feared and obeyed him, and his actions were always decisive, so their activities were never exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu was clever and full of stratagems; the bandits feared and obeyed him, and his operations were always decisive, so their raids were never discovered.

sentences.zh: 為於湖令，有能名，太守呂文顯當時幸臣，陵詆屬縣，仲孚獨不為屈。

translations.literal: He served as Magistrate of Yuhu and gained a reputation for competence. The Administrator Lü Wenxian was a favored minister of the time and bullied the subordinate counties, but Zhongfu alone would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: As Magistrate of Yuhu he earned a reputation for ability. Administrator Lü Wenxian, a court favorite of the day, bullied the subordinate counties, but Zhongfu alone refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝踐阼，復為山陰令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne, Zhongfu again served as Magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang ascended the throne, Zhongfu was again appointed Magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 仲孚長於撥煩，善適權變，吏人敬服，號稱神明，政為天下第一。

translations.literal: Zhongfu excelled at cutting through vexations and was skilled at adapting to circumstances; clerks and people revered him, calling him divine, and his governance was ranked first under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu excelled at cutting through tangled affairs and adapting flexibly to circumstances; officials and commoners alike revered him, calling him miraculous, and his administration was ranked the finest in the realm.

sentences.zh: 後為衛尉卿，恩任甚厚。

translations.literal: Later he became Commandant of the Guards and received very generous favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Commandant of the Guards and enjoyed the emperor's deep favor and trust.

sentences.zh: 初起雙闕，以仲孚領大匠，累遷豫章內史，在郡更勵清節。

translations.literal: When the twin palaces were first raised, Zhongfu was put in charge as Master of Works; he was repeatedly promoted to Internal Administrator of Yuzhang, where in the commandery he further cultivated integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When construction began on the twin palace gates, Zhongfu was appointed Master of Works; he rose through successive promotions to Internal Administrator of Yuzhang, where he redoubled his commitment to integrity.

sentences.zh: 頃之卒，贈給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he died and was posthumously awarded the title of Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate in Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously awarded the title of Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate in Attendance.

sentences.zh: 喪將還，豫章老幼號哭攀送，車輪不得前。

translations.literal: As the coffin was about to be returned, old and young of Yuzhang wailed and clung to the procession so that the wheels could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When his coffin was borne home, old and young throughout Yuzhang wailed and clung to the procession so that the wheels could not move forward.

sentences.zh: 仲孚為左丞，撰皇典二十卷，南宮故事百卷，又撰尚書具事雜儀行於世。

translations.literal: As Left Vice Director, Zhongfu compiled twenty juan of Imperial Canons, one hundred juan of Southern Palace Precedents, and also wrote Miscellaneous Rites of the Director of Documents in Full Detail, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: As Left Vice Director he compiled twenty juan of Imperial Canons and one hundred juan of Southern Palace Precedents, and also wrote Miscellaneous Rites of the Director of Documents in Full Detail, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 檀超字悅祖，高平金鄉人也。

translations.literal: Tan Chao, styled Yuezu, was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Chao, styled Yuezu, was a native of Jinxiang in Gaoping commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖嶷之字弘宗，宋南琅邪太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yingzhi, styled Hongzong, was Administrator of Southern Langye under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yingzhi, styled Hongzong, served as Administrator of Southern Langye under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父道彪字萬壽，位正員郎。

translations.literal: His father Daobiao, styled Wanshou, held the post of Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daobiao, styled Wanshou, held the post of Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 超少好文學，放誕任氣，解褐州西曹。

translations.literal: Chao from youth loved literature, was unrestrained and followed his temper, and upon leaving the cloth served as Western Clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chao loved literature; unrestrained and headstrong, he entered service as Western Clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 蕭惠開為別駕，超便抗禮。

translations.literal: When Xiao Huikai was Vice Governor, Chao treated him as an equal in ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Huikai served as Vice Governor, Chao treated him as an equal rather than a superior.

sentences.zh: 惠開自以地位居前，稍相陵辱，而超舉動嘯傲，不以地勢推之，張目謂曰：「我與卿俱是國家微賤時外戚耳，何足以一爵高人！

translations.literal: Huikai, considering his rank superior, somewhat insulted him, but Chao in his conduct was proud and defiant, not deferring on account of status. He glared and said: "You and I are both kin of the imperial house from the days when the state was still humble—what entitles you to look down on someone because of a title!"
translations.idiomatic: Huikai, considering himself the senior in rank, treated him with some condescension, but Chao carried himself with proud defiance and refused to defer. He glared at him and said, "You and I are both imperial in-laws from the days when the house was still obscure—what gives you the right to lord a mere title over another man!"

sentences.zh: 」蕭太后，惠開之祖姑，長沙景王妃，超祖姑也，故超以此議之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xiao was Huikai's great-aunt by marriage, consort of Prince Jing of Changsha, and Chao's great-aunt as well; hence Chao argued on this basis.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiao was Huikai's great-aunt by marriage—consort of Prince Jing of Changsha—and Chao's great-aunt as well, which was why Chao pressed this argument.

sentences.zh: 惠開欣然，更為刎頸之交。

translations.literal: Huikai was delighted and they became friends willing to die for each other.
translations.idiomatic: Huikai was delighted, and they became sworn friends as close as brothers.

sentences.zh: 後位國子博士，兼左丞。

translations.literal: Later he held the post of Erudite of the Imperial University and served concurrently as Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Erudite of the Imperial University and concurrently as Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 超嗜酒，好談詠，自比晉郗超，言高平有二超，又謂人曰：「猶覺我為優也。

translations.literal: Chao loved wine and delighted in talk and verse; he compared himself to Xi Chao of Jin, saying there were two Chaos in Gaoping, and told others: "I still think I am the better one."
translations.idiomatic: Chao loved wine and delighted in conversation and poetry; he compared himself to Xi Chao of Jin, remarking that Gaoping had produced two Chaos, and told others, "I still consider myself the superior of the two."

sentences.zh: 」齊高帝賞愛之，後為司徒右長史。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi prized and favored him; later he became Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi admired and favored him; later he was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，初置史官，以超與驃騎記室江淹掌史職，上表立條例：開元紀號，不取宋年；

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, when historiographers were first established, Chao and Jiang Yan, Master of Records to the Rapid Cavalry, were put in charge of historical duties. They submitted a memorial setting forth regulations: the inaugural reign title of Qi was to be used and Song years were not to be adopted;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan, when court historiographers were first established, Chao and Jiang Yan, Master of Records to the Rapid Cavalry, were placed in charge of the historical office. They submitted regulations: the Qi inaugural reign title was to be used, and Song reign years were not to be adopted;

sentences.zh: 封爵各詳本傳，無假年表。

translations.literal: enfeoffments and titles were each to be detailed in the individual biographies, with no need for a chronological table.
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffments and titles were each to be recorded in full in the individual biographies, without relying on a chronological table.

sentences.zh: 又制著十志，多為左僕射王儉所不同。

translations.literal: They also drafted ten monographs, many of which Left Vice Director Wang Jian disputed.
translations.idiomatic: They also drafted ten monographs, many of which Left Vice Director Wang Jian opposed.

sentences.zh: 既與物多忤，史功未就，徙交州，于路見殺。

translations.literal: Having offended many people, the historical work was not completed; he was banished to Jiaozhou and was killed on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Having clashed with many colleagues, he left the historical project unfinished; he was banished to Jiaozhou and was murdered on the journey.

sentences.zh: 江淹撰成之，猶不備也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yan completed the work, yet it was still not comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan finished the compilation, but it remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 時有豫章熊襄著齊典，上起十代，其序云：「尚書堯典謂之虞書，則附所述通謂之齊書，名為河洛金匱。」

translations.literal: At the time Xiong Xiang of Yuzhang wrote a Qi Canon beginning ten generations back; its preface said: "The Canon of Yao in the Documents is called the Book of Yu; likewise what is appended to what is narrated may collectively be called the Book of Qi, entitled Golden Casket of the River and Luo."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiong Xiang of Yuzhang wrote a Qi Canon reaching back ten generations; its preface read: "The Canon of Yao in the Documents is called the Book of Yu; likewise what is appended to the narrative may collectively be called the Book of Qi, entitled Golden Casket of the River and Luo."

sentences.zh: 又有吳邁遠者，好為篇章，宋明帝聞而召之。

translations.literal: There was also Wu Maiyuan, who loved composing literary pieces; Emperor Ming of Song heard of him and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wu Maiyuan, who loved composing literary pieces; Emperor Ming of Song heard of him and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 及見曰：「此人連絕之外，無所復有。

translations.literal: When he saw him he said: "This man is beyond all connection—there is nothing left of him."
translations.idiomatic: When he met him the emperor said, "This man stands utterly beyond the pale—there is nothing to him at all."

sentences.zh: 」邁遠好自誇而蚩鄙他人，每作詩，得稱意語，輒擲地呼曰：「曹子建何足數哉！

translations.literal: Maiyuan loved to boast of himself and despised others as crude; whenever he composed a poem and hit a phrase he liked, he would throw it to the ground and cry: "What is Cao Zijian worth counting!"
translations.idiomatic: Maiyuan loved to boast and held others in contempt; whenever he wrote a poem and struck a line that pleased him, he would fling it to the ground and cry, "What is Cao Zijian beside me!"

sentences.zh: 」超聞而笑曰：「昔劉季緒才不逮于作者，而好抵訶人文章。

translations.literal: Chao heard this and laughed, saying: "In the past Liu Jixu was not the equal of real writers, yet loved to criticize others' compositions."
translations.idiomatic: Chao heard this and laughed, saying, "Long ago Liu Jixu was no match for real writers, yet loved to pick apart other people's work."

sentences.zh: 季緒瑣瑣，焉足道哉，至於邁遠，何為者乎。」

translations.literal: Jixu was petty—how could he be worth mentioning? As for Maiyuan, what is he even doing?"
translations.idiomatic: Jixu was a petty man scarcely worth mentioning; as for Maiyuan, what business does he have making such claims?"

sentences.zh: 超叔父道鸞字萬安，位國子博士、永嘉太守，亦有文學，撰續晉陽秋二十卷。

translations.literal: Chao's uncle Daoluan, styled Wan'an, held the posts of Erudite of the Imperial University and Administrator of Yongjia; he too had literary talent and wrote twenty juan of a Continuation of the Jin Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's uncle Daoluan, styled Wan'an, served as Erudite of the Imperial University and Administrator of Yongjia; he too was a man of letters and wrote twenty juan of a Continuation of the Jin Annals.

sentences.zh: 卞彬字士蔚，濟陰冤句人也。

translations.literal: Bian Bin, styled Shiwei, was a native of Yuanju in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Bin, styled Shiwei, was a native of Yuanju in Jiyin commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖嗣之，中領軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sizhi was Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sizhi served as Central Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 父延之，弱冠為上虞令，有剛氣。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi, in his early twenties, was Magistrate of Shangyu and had a stern spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi, while still in his early twenties, served as Magistrate of Shangyu and was known for his unyielding character.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守孟顗以令長裁之，積不能容，脫幘投地曰：「我所以屈卿者，政為此幘耳。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Kuaiji, Meng Yan, used the authority of a district magistrate to restrain him; unable to bear it any longer, Yanzhi tore off his headcloth and threw it on the ground, saying: "The reason I humbled myself before you was precisely for this headcloth."
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji Administrator Meng Yan used his authority as district magistrate to keep him in check; at last unable to endure it, Yanzhi tore off his headcloth and flung it to the ground, saying, "The only reason I humbled myself before you was for this headcloth."

sentences.zh: 今已投之卿矣。

translations.literal: Now I have thrown it to you."
translations.idiomatic: Now I have thrown it to you."

sentences.zh: 卿以一世勳門，而傲天下國士。

translations.literal: You, from a house of merit through the ages, yet look down on the worthy men of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: You come from a house of merit through the ages, yet you look down on the worthy men of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」拂衣而去。

translations.literal: He brushed his robes and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed his robes and walked away.

sentences.zh: 彬險拔有才，而與物多忤。

translations.literal: Bin was sharp and outstanding in talent but clashed with many people.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was sharp-witted and talented, but he clashed with many people.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝輔政，袁粲、劉彥節、王蘊等皆不同，而沈攸之又稱兵反。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi served as regent, Yuan Can, Liu Yanjie, Wang Yun, and others all opposed him, while Shen Youzhi again raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi served as regent, Yuan Can, Liu Yanjie, Wang Yun, and others all opposed him, while Shen Youzhi once again took up arms in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 粲、蘊雖敗，攸之尚存。

translations.literal: Though Can and Yun were defeated, Youzhi still survived.
translations.idiomatic: Though Can and Yun had been defeated, Youzhi was still at large.

sentences.zh: 彬意猶以高帝事無所成，乃謂帝曰：「比聞謠雲'可憐可念屍著服，孝子不在日代哭，列管暫鳴死滅族'。

translations.literal: Bin still thought the emperor's affairs would come to nothing and said to him: "I have lately heard a ballad that runs, 'Pitiable, lamentable—a corpse in mourning dress; the filial son is not there, another weeps in his stead; the reed-pipe sounds briefly, then the clan is extinguished.'"
translations.idiomatic: Bin still believed the emperor's cause would fail and said to him, "I have lately heard a ballad that runs, 'Pitiable, lamentable—a corpse in mourning dress; the filial son is absent, another weeps in his place; the reed-pipe sounds briefly, then the clan is wiped out.'"

sentences.zh: 公頗聞不？

translations.literal: Have you heard it at all?"
translations.idiomatic: Have you heard anything of it?"

sentences.zh: 」時蘊居父憂，與粲同死，故云：「屍著服。

translations.literal: At that time Yun was in mourning for his father and died with Can, hence the line "a corpse in mourning dress."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Yun was in mourning for his father and died alongside Yuan Can, hence the line about a corpse in mourning dress.

translations.literal: That is what it means."
translations.idiomatic: That is what it refers to."

sentences.zh: 「服」者，衣也。

translations.literal: "Dress" means clothing."
translations.idiomatic: "Dress" means clothing."

sentences.zh: 」孝子不在日代哭。

translations.literal: "The filial son is not there, another weeps in his stead."
translations.idiomatic: "The filial son is not there, another weeps in his place."

sentences.zh: 」者，褚字也。

translations.literal: This refers to the character Chu."
translations.idiomatic: This refers to the character for Chu."

sentences.zh: 彬謂沈攸之得志，褚彥回當敗，故言哭也。

translations.literal: Bin believed that if Shen Youzhi succeeded, Chu Yanhui would be defeated, hence the mention of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Bin believed that if Shen Youzhi prevailed, Chu Yanhui would fall, hence the reference to weeping.

sentences.zh: 列管謂蕭也。

translations.literal: "Reed-pipe" refers to Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: "Reed-pipe" refers to the Xiao clan.

sentences.zh: 高帝不悅，及彬退，曰：「彬自作此。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, and when Bin had withdrawn he said: "Bin made this up himself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, and when Bin had left he said, "Bin invented this himself."

sentences.zh: 」後常於東府謁高帝，高帝時為齊王。

translations.literal: Later he often called on the emperor at the Eastern Mansion; the emperor was then Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he often called on the emperor at the Eastern Mansion, when the emperor was still Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 彬曰：「殿下即東宮為府，則以青溪為鴻溝，鴻溝以東為齊，以西為宋。

translations.literal: Bin said: "Your Highness, if the Eastern Palace becomes a separate establishment, then take Qingxi as the Hong Canal—east of the Hong Canal shall be Qi, west of it Song."
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "Your Highness, if the Eastern Palace becomes a separate establishment, then let Qingxi serve as the Hong Canal—east of the canal shall be Qi, west of it Song."

sentences.zh: 」仍詠詩云：「誰謂宋遠，跂予望之。

translations.literal: He then recited a poem: "Who says Song is far? I stand on tiptoe and gaze toward it."
translations.idiomatic: He then recited a poem: "Who says Song is far? I stand on tiptoe and gaze toward it."

sentences.zh: 」遂大忤旨，因此擯廢數年，不得仕進。

translations.literal: This greatly offended the imperial will, and for this reason he was cast aside for several years and could not advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: This deeply offended the emperor, and for several years he was cast aside and barred from office.

sentences.zh: 乃擬趙壹窮鳥為枯魚賦以喻意。

translations.literal: He then modeled himself on Zhao Yi's Impoverished Bird and wrote a Rhapsody on a Dried Fish to express his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He then modeled himself on Zhao Yi's Impoverished Bird and wrote a Rhapsody on a Dried Fish to voice his frustration.

sentences.zh: 後為南康郡丞。

translations.literal: Later he served as Assistant Administrator of Nankang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Assistant Administrator of Nankang commandery.

sentences.zh: 彬頗飲酒，擯棄形骸，仕既不遂，乃著蚤虱、蝸蟲、蝦蟆等賦，皆大有指斥。

translations.literal: Bin drank heavily and cast off all regard for propriety; his career having failed, he wrote rhapsodies on fleas and lice, snails and worms, frogs, and the like, all with sharp satirical intent.
translations.idiomatic: Bin drank heavily and cast off all regard for propriety; when his career failed to prosper, he wrote rhapsodies on fleas and lice, snails and worms, frogs, and the like, all laden with pointed satire.

sentences.zh: 其蚤虱賦序曰：「余居貧，布衣十年不制，一袍之縕，有生所托，資其寒暑，無與易之。

translations.literal: The preface to his Rhapsody on Fleas and Lice says: "I live in poverty; for ten years I have worn no new cloth garments. A single worn robe is what my life depends on; it shields me from cold and heat, and I have nothing to exchange for it."
translations.idiomatic: The preface to his Rhapsody on Fleas and Lice reads: "I live in poverty; for ten years I have worn no new cloth garments. A single threadbare robe is all my life depends on; it shields me from cold and heat, and I have nothing to replace it."

sentences.zh: 為人多病，起居甚疏，縈寢敗絮，不能自釋。

translations.literal: I am often ill and careless in my daily habits; tattered bedding clings to my sleep and I cannot free myself from it.
translations.idiomatic: I am often ill and careless in my habits; tattered bedding clings to my sleep and I cannot free myself from it.

sentences.zh: 兼攝性懈墮，懶事皮膚，澡刷不謹，澣沐失時。

translations.literal: Moreover my nature is slack and indolent; I am lazy about tending my skin, careless in bathing and scrubbing, and untimely in washing my hair.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my nature is slack and indolent; I am lazy about tending my body, careless in bathing, and irregular in washing my hair.

sentences.zh: 四體獰獰，加以臭穢，故葦席蓬纓之間，蚤虱猥流。

translations.literal: My limbs are unkempt and foul-smelling besides, so between my rush mat and coarse headband fleas and lice swarm in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: My limbs are unkempt and foul besides, so between my rush mat and coarse headband fleas and lice swarm in profusion.

sentences.zh: 淫癢渭濩，無時恕肉，探揣擭撮，日不替手。

translations.literal: Itching floods like the Wei and Hu rivers; my flesh knows no respite; groping, pinching, and plucking go on without cease from day to day.
translations.idiomatic: Itching floods without end; my flesh knows no respite; groping, pinching, and plucking go on without cease, day after day.

sentences.zh: 虱有諺言，'朝生暮孫'，若吾之虱者，無湯沐之慮，絕相吊之憂，晏聚乎久褲爛布之裳，復不懃於討捕，孫孫子子，三十五歲焉。

translations.literal: Lice have a proverb: 'Born in the morning, grandchildren by evening.' As for my lice, they need not fear hot baths, nor grieve when kin die; they dwell at ease in long-worn trousers and rotting cloth, and since I am not diligent in hunting them down, generation after generation they have lived to thirty-five years.
translations.idiomatic: Lice have a proverb: 'Born in the morning, grandchildren by evening.' My lice need fear no hot baths and grieve no deaths among their kin; they dwell at ease in long-worn trousers and rotting cloth, and since I am not diligent in hunting them down, generation after generation they have lived to thirty-five years.

sentences.zh: 」其略言皆實錄也。

translations.literal: In brief, what he wrote was all factual record.
translations.idiomatic: In brief, what he wrote was all sober fact.

sentences.zh: 又為禽獸決錄。

translations.literal: He also wrote a Judgmental Record of Birds and Beasts.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote a Judgmental Record of Birds and Beasts.

sentences.zh: 目禽獸云：「羊性淫而佷，豬性卑而率，鵝性頑而傲，狗性險而出。

translations.literal: He characterized birds and beasts thus: "Sheep are lustful and obstinate; pigs are base and rash; geese are stubborn and proud; dogs are treacherous and aggressive."
translations.idiomatic: He characterized birds and beasts thus: "Sheep are lustful and obstinate; pigs are base and rash; geese are stubborn and proud; dogs are treacherous and aggressive."

sentences.zh: 」皆指斥貴勢。

translations.literal: All were aimed at denouncing the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: All were aimed at denouncing the powerful.

sentences.zh: 其羊淫佷，謂呂文顯；

translations.literal: The lustful and obstinate sheep referred to Lü Wenxian;
translations.idiomatic: The lustful, obstinate sheep referred to Lü Wenxian;

sentences.zh: 豬卑率，謂朱隆之；

translations.literal: the base and rash pig to Zhu Longzhi;
translations.idiomatic: the base, rash pig to Zhu Longzhi;

sentences.zh: 鵝頑傲，謂潘敞；

translations.literal: the stubborn and proud goose to Pan Chang;
translations.idiomatic: the stubborn, proud goose to Pan Chang;

sentences.zh: 狗險出，謂文度。

translations.literal: the treacherous and aggressive dog to Wendu.
translations.idiomatic: the treacherous, aggressive dog to Wendu.

sentences.zh: 其險詣如此。

translations.literal: His satirical barbs were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His satirical barbs ran to this pitch.

sentences.zh: 蝦蟆賦云：「紆青拖紫，名為蛤魚。

translations.literal: His Rhapsody on the Frog says: "Trailing green and dragging purple, its name is clam-fish."
translations.idiomatic: His Rhapsody on the Frog says: "Trailing green and dragging purple, its name is clam-fish."

sentences.zh: 」世謂比令僕也。

translations.literal: The world said this compared to the Vice Directors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said this compared to the Vice Directors of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又云：「蝌鬥唯唯，群浮闇水，唯朝繼夕，聿役如鬼。

translations.literal: He also wrote: "Tadpoles murmur and murmur, floating in shoals through dark waters, serving from dawn to dusk like ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Tadpoles murmur and murmur, floating in shoals through dark waters, serving from dawn to dusk like ghosts."

sentences.zh: 」比令史諮事也。

translations.literal: This compared to the clerks and advisory attendants.
translations.idiomatic: This compared to the clerks and advisory attendants.

sentences.zh: 文章傳於閭巷。

translations.literal: His writings circulated in the lanes and alleys.
translations.idiomatic: His writings circulated widely in the streets.

sentences.zh: 後曆尚書比部郎，安吉令，車騎記室。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue for Comparisons, Magistrate of Anji, and Master of Records to the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served successively as Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue for Comparisons, Magistrate of Anji, and Master of Records to the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 彬性好飲酒，以瓠壺瓢勺杬皮為具，著帛冠，十二年不改易。

translations.literal: Bin loved wine by nature and used gourds, ladles, spoons, and elm-bark vessels as his drinking ware; he wore a cloth cap and did not change it for twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: Bin loved wine by nature and drank from gourds, ladles, spoons, and elm-bark vessels; he wore a cloth cap and did not change it for twelve years.

sentences.zh: 以大瓠為火籠，什物多諸詭異。

translations.literal: He used a large gourd as a brazier, and his household goods were mostly bizarre and eccentric.
translations.idiomatic: He used a large gourd as a brazier, and his household goods were mostly bizarre and eccentric.

sentences.zh: 自稱卞田居，婦為傅蠶室。

translations.literal: He called himself Hermit Bian of the Fields, and styled his wife Mistress of the Silkworm Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He called himself Hermit Bian of the Fields, and styled his wife Mistress of the Silkworm Chamber.

sentences.zh: 或謂曰：「卿都不持操，名器何由得升？

translations.literal: Someone said to him: "You hold to no standards at all—how can you hope to rise to honored office?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him, "You hold to no standards at all—how can you hope to rise to honored office?"

sentences.zh: 」彬曰：「擲五木子，十擲輒鞬，豈復是擲子之拙。

translations.literal: Bin said: "When I throw the five gaming pieces, I get a full house ten throws out of ten—is that really the fault of the pieces?"
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "When I throw the five gaming pieces, I get a full house ten throws out of ten—is that really the fault of the dice?"

sentences.zh: 吾好擲，政極此耳。

translations.literal: Bin said: "I love to throw them—that is simply how it is."
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "I love to throw them—that is simply how it is."

sentences.zh: 」後為綏建太守，卒官。

translations.literal: Later he became Administrator of Suijian and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Administrator of Suijian and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 永明中，琅邪諸葛勖為國子生，作雲中賦，指祭酒以下，皆有形似之目。

translations.literal: During Yongming, Zhuge Xu of Langye, a student of the Imperial University, wrote a Rhapsody from Within the Clouds, assigning to the Libationer and those below likenesses by appearance.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, Zhuge Xu of Langye, a student of the Imperial University, wrote a Rhapsody from Within the Clouds, assigning to the Libationer and those below likenesses based on their appearance.

sentences.zh: 坐事系東冶，作東冶徒賦。

translations.literal: For an offense he was imprisoned in the Eastern Works and wrote a Rhapsody of a Prisoner of the Eastern Works.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was imprisoned in the Eastern Works and wrote a Rhapsody of a Prisoner of the Eastern Works.

sentences.zh: 武帝見，赦之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu saw it, he pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu read it, he pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 又有陳郡袁嘏，自重其文，謂人云：「我詩應須大材迮之，不爾飛去。

translations.literal: There was also Yuan Ha of Chen commandery, who prized his own writing highly and told people: "My poetry needs great talent to hold it down, or else it will fly away."
translations.idiomatic: There was also Yuan Ha of Chen commandery, who prized his own poetry highly and told people, "My poems need a great talent to weigh them down, or else they will fly away."

sentences.zh: 」建武末，為諸暨令，被王敬則賊所殺。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu he was Magistrate of Zhuji and was killed by the bandits of Wang Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jianwu he served as Magistrate of Zhuji and was killed by the rebels of Wang Jingze.

sentences.zh: 時有廣陵高爽，博學多材。

translations.literal: At the time there was Gao Shuang of Guangling, learned and richly talented.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Gao Shuang of Guangling, a man of broad learning and many talents.

sentences.zh: 劉蒨為晉陵縣，爽經途詣之，了不相接，爽甚銜之。

translations.literal: When Liu Qian was magistrate of Jinling, Shuang passed through and called on him but received no welcome at all; Shuang deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qian was magistrate of Jinling, Shuang passed through and called on him but received no welcome at all; Shuang deeply resented the snub.

sentences.zh: 俄而爽代蒨為縣，蒨遣迎贈甚厚。

translations.literal: Before long Shuang replaced Qian as magistrate, and Qian sent generous gifts to welcome and honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shuang replaced Qian as magistrate, and Qian sent generous gifts to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 爽受餉，答書云：「高晉陵自答。

translations.literal: Shuang accepted the gifts and replied in a letter: "Gao of Jinling will answer for himself."
translations.idiomatic: Shuang accepted the gifts and replied in a letter: "Gao of Jinling will answer for himself."

sentences.zh: 」人問其所以，答云：「劉蒨餉晉陵令耳，何關爽事。

translations.literal: When people asked his reason, he answered: "Liu Qian was making gifts to the magistrate of Jinling—what has that to do with Shuang?"
translations.idiomatic: When people asked his reason, he answered, "Liu Qian was making gifts to the magistrate of Jinling—what has that to do with me?"

sentences.zh: 」又有人送書與爽告躓，云：「比日守羊困苦。

translations.literal: Someone also sent Shuang a letter reporting a mishap, saying: "Lately guarding the sheep has been hard going."
translations.idiomatic: Someone also sent Shuang a letter reporting a mishap, saying, "Lately guarding the sheep has been hard going."

sentences.zh: 」爽答曰：「守羊無食，何不貨羊糴米。

translations.literal: Shuang replied: "If guarding sheep brings no food, why not sell the sheep and buy grain?"
translations.idiomatic: Shuang replied, "If guarding sheep brings no food, why not sell the sheep and buy grain?"

sentences.zh: 」孫抱為延陵縣，爽又詣之，抱了無故人之懷。

translations.literal: When Sun Bao was magistrate of Yanling, Shuang called on him again, but Bao showed none of the warmth due an old acquaintance.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Bao was magistrate of Yanling, Shuang called on him again, but Bao showed none of the warmth due an old friend.

sentences.zh: 爽出從縣合下過，取筆書鼓云：「徒有八尺圍，腹無一寸腸，面皮如許厚，受打未詎央。

translations.literal: As Shuang left he passed beneath the county gate drum, took up a brush, and wrote on it: "Eight feet around in girth, yet not an inch of gut within; skin and flesh so thick—beatings never reach the core."
translations.idiomatic: As Shuang left he passed beneath the county gate drum, took up a brush, and wrote on it: "Eight feet around in girth, yet not an inch of gut within; skin so thick—beatings never reach the core."

sentences.zh: 」爽機悟多如此。

translations.literal: Shuang's quick wit showed itself in many such ways.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang's quick wit showed itself in many such ways.

sentences.zh: 坐事被系，作鑊魚賦以自況，其文甚工。

translations.literal: For an offense he was imprisoned and wrote a Rhapsody on the Cauldron Fish to portray his situation; the piece was very finely wrought.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was imprisoned and wrote a Rhapsody on the Cauldron Fish to portray his situation; the piece was finely wrought.

sentences.zh: 後遇赦免，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was pardoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was pardoned and died.

sentences.zh: 抱東莞人。

translations.literal: Bao was a native of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was a native of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 父廉，吳興太守。

translations.literal: His father Lian was Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lian served as Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 抱善吏職，形體肥壯，腰帶十圍，爽故以此激之。

translations.literal: Bao was skilled in administrative duties; his body was stout and robust, his belt ten arm-spans around, and Shuang therefore used this to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was skilled in administrative duties; his body was stout and robust, his belt ten arm-spans around, and Shuang therefore used this to mock him.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，桂陽王休范在尋陽，以巨源有筆翰，遣船迎之，餉以錢物。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui, the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan, was at Xunyang; because Juyuan had literary talent, he sent a boat to fetch him and presented him with money and goods.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhui, the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan, was at Xunyang; because Juyuan had literary talent, he sent a boat to fetch him and presented him with money and goods.

sentences.zh: 巨源因齊高帝自啟，敕板起之，使留都下。

translations.literal: Juyuan reported this through Emperor Gao of Qi, who ordered him summoned by official appointment and kept at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan reported this through Emperor Gao of Qi, who ordered him summoned by official appointment and kept at the capital.

sentences.zh: 桂陽事起，使於中書省撰符檄，事平，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: When the Guiyang affair broke out, he was assigned to draft proclamations and summons at the Secretariat; when the matter was settled, he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guiyang affair broke out, he was assigned to draft proclamations and summons at the Secretariat; when the matter was settled, he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance.

sentences.zh: 巨源望有封賞，既而不獲，乃與尚書令袁粲書自陳，竟不被申。

translations.literal: Juyuan hoped for enfeoffment and reward but did not receive them; he then wrote to Director of the Secretariat Yuan Can to plead his own case, yet in the end his petition was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan hoped for enfeoffment and reward but received none; he then wrote to Director of the Secretariat Yuan Can to plead his case, yet in the end his petition went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事，高帝又使為尚書符荊州，以此又望賞異，自此意常不滿。

translations.literal: During the affair of Shen Youzhi, the emperor again had him draft the Secretariat dispatch to Jingzhou; for this he again hoped for special reward, and from then on his mind was often discontented.
translations.idiomatic: During the affair of Shen Youzhi, the emperor again had him draft the Secretariat dispatch to Jingzhou; for this he again hoped for special reward, and from then on he was often discontented.

sentences.zh: 後除武昌太守，拜竟，不樂江外行。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Administrator of Wuchang; when the appointment was announced, he took no pleasure in traveling beyond the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Administrator of Wuchang; when the appointment was announced, he took no pleasure in traveling beyond the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 武帝問之，巨源曰：「古人云，'甯飲建鄴水，不食武昌魚'。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu asked him, Juyuan said: "The ancients said, 'Better drink the waters of Jiankang than eat the fish of Wuchang.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu asked him, Juyuan said, "The ancients said, 'Better drink the waters of Jiankang than eat the fish of Wuchang.'"

sentences.zh: 臣年已老，甯死於建鄴。

translations.literal: I am already old and would rather die in Jiankang."
translations.idiomatic: I am already old and would rather die in Jiankang."

sentences.zh: 」乃以為余杭令。

translations.literal: He was therefore appointed Magistrate of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore appointed Magistrate of Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 明帝為吳興，巨源作秋胡詩，有譏刺語，以事見殺。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was in Wuxing, Juyuan wrote a poem on Qiuhu containing satirical language and was executed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was in Wuxing, Juyuan wrote a poem on Qiuhu containing satirical language and was executed on that account.

sentences.zh: 時又有會稽孔廣、孔逭皆才學知名。

translations.literal: At the time there were also Kong Guang and Kong Huan of Kuaiji, both renowned for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were also Kong Guang and Kong Huan of Kuaiji, both renowned for talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 廣字淹源，美容止，善吐論。

translations.literal: Guang, styled Yanyuan, had a handsome bearing and was skilled at discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, styled Yanyuan, had a handsome bearing and was skilled at discourse.

sentences.zh: 王儉、張緒咸美之。

translations.literal: Wang Jian and Zhang Xu both admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian and Zhang Xu both admired him.

sentences.zh: 儉常云：「廣來使人廢簿領，匠不須來，來則莫聽去。

translations.literal: Jian often said: "When Guang comes, he makes one abandon one's paperwork; craftsmen need not come—if they do, do not let them leave."
translations.idiomatic: Jian often said, "When Guang visits, he makes one abandon one's paperwork; craftsmen need not come—and if they do, do not let them leave."

sentences.zh: 」緒數巾車詣之，每歎云：「孔廣使吾成輕薄祭酒。

translations.literal: Xu repeatedly came to visit him in a cloth-canopied carriage and would sigh: "Kong Guang makes me into a frivolous Libationer."
translations.idiomatic: Xu repeatedly came to visit him in a cloth-canopied carriage and would sigh, "Kong Guang turns me into a frivolous Libationer."

sentences.zh: 」仕至揚州中從事。

translations.literal: In office he rose to Attendant of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In office he rose to Attendant of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 逭抗直有才藻，制東都賦，于時才士稱之。

translations.literal: Huan was upright and forthright with literary gifts; he composed a Rhapsody on the Eastern Capital, which the talented men of the time praised.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was upright and forthright with literary gifts; he composed a Rhapsody on the Eastern Capital, which the talented men of the time praised.

sentences.zh: 陳郡謝瀹年少時遊會稽還，父莊問：「入東何見，見孔逭不？

translations.literal: When Xie Yue of Chen commandery returned from traveling in Kuaiji in his youth, his father Zhuang asked: "What did you see in the east—did you see Kong Huan?"
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Yue of Chen commandery returned from traveling in Kuaiji in his youth, his father Zhuang asked, "What did you see in the east—did you meet Kong Huan?"

sentences.zh: 」見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 著三吳決錄，不傳。

translations.literal: He wrote a Record of the Three Wu, which has not been transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a Record of the Three Wu, which has not survived.

sentences.zh: 終於衛軍武陵王東曹掾。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Eastern Bureau Attendant to the Prince of Wuling, General of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Eastern Bureau Attendant to the Prince of Wuling, General of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 又時有虞通之、虞和、司馬憲、袁仲明、孫詵等，皆有學行，與廣埒名。

translations.literal: At the time there were also Yu Tongzhi, Yu He, Sima Xian, Yuan Zhongming, Sun Shen, and others, all of learning and conduct, whose fame matched Guang's.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were also Yu Tongzhi, Yu He, Sima Xian, Yuan Zhongming, Sun Shen, and others, all men of learning and integrity whose fame matched Guang's.

sentences.zh: 通之、和皆會稽余姚人，通之善言易，至步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Tongzhi and He were both natives of Yuyao in Kuaiji; Tongzhi was skilled in expounding the Changes and rose to Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi and He were both natives of Yuyao in Kuaiji; Tongzhi was skilled in expounding the Changes and rose to Colonel of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 和位中書郎、廷尉，少好學，居貧屋漏，恐濕墳典，乃舒被覆書，書獲全而被大濕。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Secretariat Gentleman and Commandant of Justice; from youth he loved learning. His dwelling was poor and leaked; fearing his classical texts would be dampened, he spread his quilt over the books—the books were preserved but the quilt was thoroughly soaked.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Secretariat Gentleman and Commandant of Justice; from youth he loved learning. His dwelling was poor and leaked; fearing his classical texts would be ruined by damp, he spread his quilt over the books—the books were preserved but the quilt was thoroughly soaked.

sentences.zh: 時人以比高鳳。

translations.literal: People of the time compared him to Gao Feng.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time compared him to Gao Feng.

sentences.zh: 憲字景思，河內溫人，待詔東觀為學士，至殿中郎，口辯有才地，使魏見稱於北。

translations.literal: Xian, styled Jingsi, was a native of Wen in Henei; he awaited imperial commands at the Eastern Pavilion as a scholar, rose to Palace Attendant, was eloquent and talented, and on a mission to Wei won praise in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, styled Jingsi, was a native of Wen in Henei; he served as a scholar awaiting commands at the Eastern Pavilion, rose to Palace Attendant, was eloquent and talented, and on a mission to Wei won praise in the north.

sentences.zh: 仲明，陳郡人，撰晉史，未成而卒。

translations.literal: Zhongming was a native of Chen commandery; he compiled a History of Jin but died before completing it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongming was a native of Chen commandery; he compiled a History of Jin but died before completing it.

sentences.zh: 初仲明與劉融、卞鑠俱為袁粲所賞，恒在坐席。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhongming, together with Liu Rong and Bian Shuo, had all been favored by Yuan Can and were constantly among his seated company.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhongming, together with Liu Rong and Bian Shuo, had all been favored by Yuan Can and were constantly among his seated company.

sentences.zh: 粲為丹陽尹，取鑠為主簿。

translations.literal: When Can became Intendant of Danyang, he appointed Shuo as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Can took office as Intendant of Danyang, he appointed Bian Shuo as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 好詩賦，多譏刺世人，坐徙巴州。

translations.literal: He loved poetry and fu, often satirized people of the age, and for this was banished to Ba province.
translations.idiomatic: He loved poetry and rhapsodies and often satirized his contemporaries; for this he was banished to Ba province.

sentences.zh: 詵字休群，太原中都人，愛文，尤賞泉石。

translations.literal: Shen, styled Xiuqun, was a native of Zhongdu in Taiyuan; he loved literature and especially appreciated springs and rocks.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shen, styled Xiuqun, was a native of Zhongdu in Taiyuan. He loved letters and had a special fondness for springs and rocky landscapes.

sentences.zh: 卒于御史中丞。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Vice Director of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Vice Director of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 王智深字雲才，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhishen, styled Yuncai, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhishen, styled Yuncai, came from Linyi in Langye commandery.

sentences.zh: 少從陳郡謝超宗學屬文。

translations.literal: From youth he studied literary composition under Xie Chaozong of Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied literary composition under Xie Chaozong of Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，拙澀乏風儀。

translations.literal: He loved drinking wine; he was awkward and unpolished and lacked grace in bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of wine, but awkward and halting in manner and lacking in dignified bearing.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為豫章王大司馬參軍，兼記室。

translations.literal: He served Qi as Senior Major to the Grand Marshal for the Prince of Yuzhang, concurrently as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi he served as senior major on the staff of the Prince of Yuzhang's grand marshal, and also as recorder.

sentences.zh: 家貧無人事，嘗餓五日不得食，掘莞根食之。

translations.literal: His family was poor and had no one to assist him; once he went hungry five days without food and dug up cattail roots to eat.
translations.idiomatic: His family was destitute and without patrons; once he went five days without food and dug up cattail roots to eat.

sentences.zh: 司空王僧虔及子志分與衣食。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wang Sengqian and his son Zhi shared food and clothing with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works Wang Sengqian and his son Zhi shared their food and clothing with him.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 崔慰祖字悅宗，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Weizu, styled Yuezong, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Weizu, styled Yuezong, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 父慶緒，永明中為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Qingxu served as Inspector of Liang province during the Yongming era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingxu served as Inspector of Liang province during the Yongming reign.

sentences.zh: 慰祖解褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: Weizu upon first taking office became a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu entered official service as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 父喪不食鹽，母曰：「汝既無兄弟，又未有子胤。

translations.literal: During his father's mourning he abstained from salt; his mother said: "You have no brothers, and as yet no sons to carry on the line.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father he abstained from salt. His mother said, "You have no brothers, and as yet no sons to carry on the family line.

sentences.zh: 毀不滅性，政當不進肴羞耳，如何絕鹽。

translations.literal: Mourning need not destroy one's nature; one need only abstain from savory dishes—how can you cut off salt entirely?
translations.idiomatic: Grief should not destroy one's life; one need only forgo rich foods. Why must you cut out salt altogether?

sentences.zh: 吾今亦不食矣。

translations.literal: From now on I too shall not eat.
translations.idiomatic: From now on I shall not eat either.

sentences.zh: 」慰祖不得已，從之。

translations.literal: " Weizu had no choice but to comply.
translations.idiomatic: " Weizu had no choice but to yield.

sentences.zh: 父梁州之資，家財千萬，散與宗族。

translations.literal: From his father's assets as Inspector of Liang, the family fortune amounted to ten million; he distributed it among the clan.
translations.idiomatic: From his father's tenure in Liang province the family had amassed a fortune of ten million cash, which he distributed among the clan.

sentences.zh: 漆器題為「日」字，「日」字之器流乎遠近。

translations.literal: Lacquerware was marked with the character "日"; vessels bearing the "日" character circulated far and near.
translations.idiomatic: He marked his lacquerware with the character ri, and pieces so marked spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 料得父時假貰文疏，謂族子紘曰：「彼有自當見還，彼無吾何言哉。

translations.literal: He gathered his father's loan documents and said to his clansman Hong: "Those who have means will repay of their own accord; as for those who lack means, what can I say?
translations.idiomatic: He collected the loan records from his father's time and said to his clansman Hong, "Those who can repay will do so on their own; as for those who cannot, what more can I say?

sentences.zh: 」悉火焚之。

translations.literal: " He burned them all in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he burned them all.

sentences.zh: 好學，聚書至萬卷。

translations.literal: He loved learning and amassed books to ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and collected books until he had ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 鄰里年少好事者來從假借，日數十帙。

translations.literal: Young men in the neighborhood who loved such pursuits would come to borrow from him, dozens of scrolls per day.
translations.idiomatic: Young neighbors fond of such things would come to borrow from him, sometimes dozens of scrolls in a single day.

sentences.zh: 慰祖親自取與，未嘗為辭。

translations.literal: Weizu personally retrieved and handed them out and never made excuses.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu personally fetched and lent them out and never refused.

sentences.zh: 為始安王遙光撫軍刑獄，兼記室。

translations.literal: He served as Judge of the Pacifying Army for Prince Shian Yao Guang, concurrently as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge on the pacifying army staff of Prince Shian Yao Guang, and also as recorder.

sentences.zh: 遙光好棋，數召慰祖對戲。

translations.literal: Yao Guang loved weiqi and repeatedly summoned Weizu to play against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guang loved the game of weiqi and often summoned Weizu to play against him.

sentences.zh: 慰祖輒辭拙，非朔望不見也。

translations.literal: Weizu always pleaded incompetence and would not appear except on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu always pleaded clumsiness at the board and would not visit except on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 建武中詔舉士，從兄慧景舉慰祖及平原劉孝標並碩學。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era an edict summoned scholars; his older paternal cousin Huijing recommended Weizu together with Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan as eminent scholars.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu era an edict called for scholars of merit; his older cousin Huijing recommended Weizu and Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan together as leading scholars.

sentences.zh: 帝欲試以百里，慰祖辭不就。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to test him with a hundred-li district, but Weizu declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to try him with a district magistracy, but Weizu declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 國子祭酒沈約、吏部郎謝朓嘗於吏部省中賓友俱集，各問慰祖地理中所不悉十餘事，慰祖口吃無華辭，而酬據精悉，一座稱服之。

translations.literal: Libationer of the National University Shen Yue and Director of Personnel Xie Tiao once gathered with guest friends in the Ministry of Personnel offices; each asked Weizu more than ten matters in geography that they did not understand. Weizu stuttered and had no flowery rhetoric, yet his replies based on evidence were precise and thorough, and the whole assembly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when Shen Yue, Libationer of the Imperial Academy, and Xie Tiao, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, gathered with friends in the personnel bureau, each put to Weizu more than a dozen geographical questions he could not answer. Weizu stuttered and spoke without flourish, yet his replies—grounded in fact—were precise and exhaustive, and everyone present was filled with admiration.

sentences.zh: 朓歎曰：「假使班、馬復生，無以過此。」

translations.literal: Xiao sighed and said: "Even if Ban and Sima were to live again, they could not surpass this."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiao sighed and said, "Even if Ban Gu and Sima Qian were reborn, they could not surpass this."

sentences.zh: 慰祖賣宅須四十五萬，買者云：「寧有減不？

translations.literal: Weizu was selling his house for four hundred fifty thousand; the buyer said: "Might there be a reduction?
translations.idiomatic: Weizu was selling his house for four hundred fifty thousand cash. The buyer asked, "Can you come down a little?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「誠異韓伯休，何容二價。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I am truly unlike Han Boyou—how could I allow two prices?
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "I am no Han Boyou—how could I set two prices?

sentences.zh: 」買者又曰：「君但賣四十六萬，一萬見與。

translations.literal: " The buyer said again: "You need only sell for four hundred sixty thousand; ten thousand I will give you directly.
translations.idiomatic: " The buyer added, "Just sell it for four hundred sixty thousand—I will give you ten thousand on the side.

sentences.zh: 」慰祖曰：「豈是我心乎？」

translations.literal: " Weizu said: "Is that what my heart desires?"
translations.idiomatic: " Weizu said, "Would that be worthy of my conscience?"

sentences.zh: 少與侍中江祀款，及祀貴，常來候之，而慰祖不往也。

translations.literal: From youth he was on intimate terms with Attendant-in-Ordinary Jiang Si; when Si rose high, he often came to visit him, but Weizu never went to see him in return.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close to Attendant-in-Ordinary Jiang Si. When Si rose to high rank he often came to call on Weizu, but Weizu never returned the visits.

sentences.zh: 與丹陽丞劉渢素善，遙光據東府反，慰祖在城內。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Assistant Magistrate of Danyang Liu Fan; when Yao Guang seized the Eastern Quarter and rebelled, Weizu was inside the city.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Liu Fan, assistant magistrate of Danyang. When Yao Guang seized the Eastern Quarter and rebelled, Weizu was inside the city.

sentences.zh: 城未潰一日，渢謂之曰：「卿有老母，宜出。

translations.literal: One day before the city fell, Fan said to him: "You have an aged mother—you should leave.
translations.idiomatic: One day before the city fell, Fan said to him, "You have an old mother. You ought to get out.

sentences.zh: 」命門者出之。

translations.literal: " He ordered the gatekeeper to let him out.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the gatekeeper to let him leave.

sentences.zh: 慰祖詣闕自首，系尚方，病卒。

translations.literal: Weizu went to the palace gate to surrender himself, was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshops, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu went to the palace to surrender himself, was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshops, and died of illness there.

sentences.zh: 慰祖著海岱志，起太公迄西晉人物，為四十卷，半成。

translations.literal: Weizu authored the Record of the Sea and Mount Tai, covering figures from the Grand Duke down through Western Jin, in forty scrolls, half finished.
translations.idiomatic: Weizu wrote the Record of the Sea and Mount Tai, treating figures from the Grand Duke down through Western Jin in forty scrolls, of which only half were completed.

sentences.zh: 臨卒，與從弟緯書云：「常欲更注遷、固二史，采史、漢所漏二百餘事，在廚簏，可檢寫之，以存大意。

translations.literal: As he lay dying, he wrote to his younger paternal cousin Wei, saying: "I have always wished to re-annotate the two histories of Qian and Gu, gathering more than two hundred matters omitted from the Records and the Book of Han; they are in the kitchen cupboard—look through them and copy them out to preserve the main ideas.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he wrote to his younger cousin Wei: "I had long wished to re-annotate Sima Qian's and Ban Gu's two histories, collecting more than two hundred items omitted from the Records and the Book of Han. The notes are in the kitchen cupboard; please search them out and copy them to preserve the main points.

sentences.zh: 海岱志良未周悉，可寫數本付護軍諸從事人一通，及友人任昉、徐寅、劉洋、裴揆，令後世知吾微有素業也。

translations.literal: The Record of the Sea and Mount Tai is truly not yet complete; make several copies and send one each to the various staff officers of the Guard General, and to my friends Ren Fang, Xu Yin, Liu Yang, and Pei Kui, so that later ages may know I had some modest scholarly legacy.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of the Sea and Mount Tai is still far from complete. Make several copies and send one to the staff officers of the Guard General, and also to my friends Ren Fang, Xu Yin, Liu Yang, and Pei Kui, so that later generations may know I had some small scholarly legacy.

sentences.zh: 」又令以棺親土，不須磚，勿設靈座。

translations.literal: " He also ordered that the coffin be placed directly upon the earth, that no bricks be used, and that no spirit seat be set up.
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered that his coffin be placed directly on the earth, without brick lining, and that no spirit seat be set up.

sentences.zh: 祖沖之字文遠，范陽遒人也。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi, styled Wenyuan, was a native of You in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi, styled Wenyuan, came from You in Fanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖台之，晉侍中。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Taizhi was a Jin Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Taizhi served the Jin as Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 祖昌，宋大匠卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang was Song Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang served the Song as Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 父朔之，奉朝請。

translations.literal: His father Shuozhi was a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuozhi was a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 沖之稽古，有機思，宋孝武使直華林學省，賜宅宇車服。

translations.literal: Chongzhi investigated antiquity and had ingenuity in mechanical contrivances; Emperor Xiaowu of Song appointed him to the Hualin Academy and granted him a residence, carriage, and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi was a scholar of antiquity with a gift for ingenious contrivances. Emperor Xiaowu of Song assigned him to the Hualin Academy and granted him a residence, carriage, and official robes.

sentences.zh: 解褐南徐州從事、公府參軍。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he became Adjunct of South Xuzhou and Staff Officer in the prince's residence.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointments were as adjutant of South Xuzhou and staff officer in a prince's household.

sentences.zh: 始元嘉中，用何承天所制曆，比古十一家為密。

translations.literal: Beginning in the Yuanjia era, the calendar devised by He Chengtian was used; compared with the eleven ancient calendars it was more precise.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yuanjia era onward the calendar devised by He Chengtian was used, and compared with the eleven ancient systems it was the most precise.

sentences.zh: 沖之以為尚疏，乃更造新法，上表言之。

translations.literal: Chongzhi considered it still too coarse and therefore devised a new method, submitting a memorial to set it forth.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi judged it still too loose and devised a new method, which he presented in a memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 孝武令朝士善曆者難之，不能屈。

translations.literal: Xiaowu had court scholars skilled in calendrics challenge him, but they could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu had court scholars versed in calendrics challenge him, but none could defeat his arguments.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩不施行。

translations.literal: But the emperor died before it could be implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died before the reform could be put into effect.

sentences.zh: 轉長水校尉，領本職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Colonel of the Changshui while retaining his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Colonel of the Changshui while retaining his original duties.

sentences.zh: 沖之造安邊論，欲開屯田，廣農殖。

translations.literal: Chongzhi composed the Treatise on Securing the Border, wishing to open military colonies and expand agricultural production.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi wrote the Treatise on Securing the Border, proposing to open military colonies and expand farming.

sentences.zh: 建武中，明帝欲使沖之巡行四方，興造大業，可以利百姓者，會連有軍事，事竟不行。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era Emperor Ming wished to have Chongzhi tour the four quarters and undertake great works that could benefit the common people, but continuous military affairs intervened and in the end it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwu era Emperor Ming wished to send Chongzhi on a tour of the realm to undertake great public works for the people's benefit, but repeated military campaigns intervened and the plan was never carried out.

sentences.zh: 沖之解鍾律博塞，當時獨絕，莫能對者。

translations.literal: Chongzhi understood bells, pitch pipes, and board games; in his time he stood alone without equal, and none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi mastered bells, pitch pipes, and board games; in his day he stood alone, and no one could match him.

sentences.zh: 以諸葛亮有木牛流馬，乃造一器，不因風水，施機自運，不勞人力。

translations.literal: Because Zhuge Liang had had the wooden ox and flowing horse, he built a device that, without relying on wind or water, applied mechanism to move itself and required no human labor.
translations.idiomatic: Inspired by Zhuge Liang's wooden ox and flowing horse, he built a device that moved by mechanism alone, without wind or water, and needed no human labor.

sentences.zh: 又造千里船，于新亭江試之，日行百餘里。

translations.literal: He also built a thousand-li boat and tested it on the Xin Pavilion river; in a day it traveled more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He also built a fast long-distance boat and tested it on the river at Xinting; in one day it covered more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 于樂游苑造水碓磨，武帝親自臨視。
