translations.literal: At the Leyou Gardens he built a water-powered pounding mill and grindstones; Emperor Wu personally came to inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: At the Leyou Gardens he built a water-powered mill and grindstones, which Emperor Wu inspected in person.

sentences.zh: 又特善算。

translations.literal: He was also especially skilled in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He was also exceptionally skilled in mathematics.

sentences.zh: 永元二年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yongyuan, at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yongyuan, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 著易老莊義，釋論語、孝經，注九章，造綴述數十篇。

translations.literal: He authored commentaries on the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, explicated the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety, annotated the Nine Chapters, and compiled several dozen treatises.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote commentaries on the Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, explications of the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety, an annotation of the Nine Chapters, and several dozen other works.

sentences.zh: 子暅之。

translations.literal: His son was Xuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xuanshi.

sentences.zh: 暅之字景爍，少傳家業，究極精微，亦有巧思。

translations.literal: Xuanshi, styled Jingshuo, from youth inherited the family profession, pursued the utmost subtlety, and also had ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanshi, styled Jingshuo, inherited the family craft from youth, pursued its subtlest depths, and possessed a gift for ingenious design.

sentences.zh: 入神之妙，般、倕無以過也。

translations.literal: In the subtlety of entering the spirit of the craft, even Gongshu Ban and Artisan Chui could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: In the subtle mastery that enters the realm of spirit, even Gongshu Ban and Artisan Chui could not surpass him.

sentences.zh: 當其詣微之時，雷霆不能入。

translations.literal: When he had attained the subtlest point, thunder could not penetrate his concentration.
translations.idiomatic: When he had reached the subtlest depths of his craft, even thunder could not break through his concentration.

sentences.zh: 嘗行遇僕射徐勉，以頭觸之，勉呼乃悟。

translations.literal: Once while walking he encountered Vice Director Xu Mian; he bumped into him with his head, and only when Mian called out did he come to his senses.
translations.idiomatic: Once while walking he ran into Vice Director Xu Mian and struck him with his head; only when Mian called out did he come to himself.

sentences.zh: 父所改何承天歷時尚未行，梁天監初，暅之更修之，於是始行焉。

translations.literal: The calendar his father had revised from He Chengtian's system had not yet been implemented; at the beginning of the Liang Tianjian era Xuanshi further revised it, and only then was it put into use.
translations.idiomatic: The calendar his father had revised from He Chengtian's system had not yet been adopted; at the start of the Liang Tianjian era Xuanshi revised it further, and only then was it put into effect.

sentences.zh: 位至太舟卿。

translations.literal: He rose to Minister of the Imperial Boats.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Minister of the Imperial Boats.

sentences.zh: 暅之子皓，志節慷慨，有文武才略。

translations.literal: Xuanshi's son Hao was ardent in integrity and generous in spirit, and possessed both civil and military talent and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanshi's son Hao was high-minded and resolute, with both literary and military gifts.

sentences.zh: 少傳家業，善算曆。

translations.literal: From youth he inherited the family profession and was skilled in calculation and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he inherited the family craft and was skilled in mathematics and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 大同中為江都令，後拜廣陵太守。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he served as Magistrate of Jiangdu, and later was appointed Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era he served as magistrate of Jiangdu, and was later appointed administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 侯景陷台城，皓在城中，將見害，乃逃歸江西。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing captured Taicheng, Hao was inside the city and about to be killed; he fled back to the region west of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing took Taicheng, Hao was inside the city and faced execution; he fled west of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 百姓感其遺惠，每相蔽匿。

translations.literal: The common people, moved by the lingering kindness of his rule, repeatedly sheltered and concealed him.
translations.idiomatic: The people, grateful for the kindness he had shown them in office, repeatedly hid and sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 廣陵人來嶷乃說皓曰：「逆豎滔天，王室如毀，正是義夫發憤之秋，志士忘軀之日。

translations.literal: Lai Yi of Guangling then urged Hao, saying: "The rebellious villain fills heaven; the royal house is as if in ruin—this is the season for righteous men to vent their anger and the day for men of resolve to forget their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Yi of Guangling then urged Hao: "The rebel fills heaven with outrage and the royal house seems near ruin. This is the season for righteous men to rise in fury and the day for men of purpose to forget their lives.

sentences.zh: 府君荷恩重世，又不為賊所容。

translations.literal: My lord has borne kindness through generations, and moreover is not tolerated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: My lord has received the dynasty's favor through generations, and the rebels will not spare you.

sentences.zh: 今逃竄草間，知者非一，危亡之甚，累棋非喻。

translations.literal: Now you flee and hide among the weeds; more than one person knows where you are—the danger of ruin is so great that piling up chess pieces cannot illustrate it.
translations.idiomatic: Now you skulk among the grass, and more than one person knows where you are. The peril is beyond comparison—no stack of chess pieces could measure it.

sentences.zh: 董紹先雖景之心腹，輕而無謀，新克此州，人情不附，襲而殺之，此一壯士之任耳。

translations.literal: Dong Shaoxian, though Hou Jing's trusted man, is frivolous and without strategy; having newly taken this province, the people's hearts are not attached to him—surprise and kill him: that is a task for a single bold warrior.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shaoxian is Hou Jing's confidant, but he is rash and unwise. He has only just taken this province and the people do not support him. A surprise attack to kill him is a task fit for one bold warrior.

sentences.zh: 今若糾率義勇，立可得三二百人。

translations.literal: If we now muster righteous volunteers, we can immediately obtain two or three hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: If we rally loyal volunteers now, we can raise two or three hundred men at once.

sentences.zh: 意欲奉戴府君，剿除凶逆，遠近義徒，自當投赴。

translations.literal: We wish to install you, my lord, to exterminate the wicked rebels; righteous followers near and far will surely rally to us.
translations.idiomatic: We mean to install you as our leader and wipe out the rebels; loyal men near and far will surely flock to our banner.

sentences.zh: 如其克捷，可立桓、文之勳；

translations.literal: If we succeed, we may establish achievements like those of Duke Huan and Duke Wen;
translations.idiomatic: If we succeed, we may win glory like that of Duke Huan and Duke Wen;

sentences.zh: 必天未悔禍，事生理外，百代之下，猶為梁室忠臣。

translations.literal: and even if Heaven has not yet repented the disaster and matters go beyond reason, a hundred generations hence you will still be a loyal minister of the house of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: and even if Heaven has not yet turned from calamity and success lies beyond reason, a hundred generations hence you will still be remembered as a loyal minister of the Liang.

sentences.zh: 若何？

translations.literal: What do you say?
translations.idiomatic: What say you?

sentences.zh: 」皓曰：「僕所願也，死且甘心。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "That is what I wish; even death I would accept gladly.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "That is what I wish. I would gladly die for it.

sentences.zh: 」為要勇士耿光等百餘人襲殺景兗州刺史董紹先，推前太子舍人蕭勉為刺史，結東魏為援。

translations.literal: " He enlisted bold warriors Geng Guang and more than a hundred others to launch a surprise attack and kill Dong Shaoxian, Hou Jing's Inspector of Yan province; he installed the former Crown Prince's Attendant Xiao Mian as inspector and allied with Eastern Wei for support.
translations.idiomatic: " He gathered bold warriors led by Geng Guang, more than a hundred in all, to launch a surprise attack and kill Dong Shaoxian, Hou Jing's inspector of Yan province. He installed the former crown prince's attendant Xiao Mian as governor and sought aid from Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 馳檄遠近，將討景。

translations.literal: He dispatched proclamations near and far, intending to campaign against Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent proclamations far and wide, preparing to march against Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 景大懼，即日率侯子鑒等攻之。

translations.literal: Hou Jing was greatly afraid and that very day led Hou Zijian and others to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing was terrified and that same day led Hou Zijian and others against him.

sentences.zh: 城陷，皓見執，被縛射之，箭遍體，然後車裂以徇。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Hao was captured, bound, and shot; arrows covered his body, and then he was dismembered by cart as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Hao was taken prisoner, bound, and shot until arrows covered his body; only then was he torn apart by chariots as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 城中無少長，皆埋而射之。

translations.literal: In the city none young or old—all were buried and shot at.
translations.idiomatic: In the city, every person, young and old alike, was buried up to the waist and shot.

sentences.zh: 來嶷字德山，幼有奇節，兼資文武。

translations.literal: Lai Yi, styled Deshan, from youth had extraordinary integrity and possessed both civil and military gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Yi, styled Deshan, showed exceptional character from youth and combined civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 既與皓義舉，邵陵王承制除步兵校尉、秦郡太守，封永甯縣侯。

translations.literal: After joining Hao's righteous uprising, the Prince of Shaoling, acting under imperial commission, appointed him Colonel of Footsoldiers and Administrator of Qin commandery, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yongning county.
translations.idiomatic: After joining Hao's loyalist rising, the Prince of Shaoling, acting under imperial commission, appointed him Colonel of Footsoldiers and administrator of Qin commandery, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 及皓敗，並兄弟子侄遇害者十六人。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, together with brothers, sons, and nephews, sixteen persons were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated, sixteen of his brothers, sons, and nephews were killed.

sentences.zh: 子法敏逃免，仕陳為海陵令。

translations.literal: His son Famin escaped and survived, and served Chen as Magistrate of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Famin escaped with his life and later served the Chen as magistrate of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 賈希鏡，平陽襄陵人也。

translations.literal: Jia Xijing was a native of Xiangling in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xijing came from Xiangling in Pingyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖弼之，晉員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bizhi was a Jin Supernumerary Official.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bizhi served the Jin as a supernumerary official.

sentences.zh: 父匪之，驃騎參軍。

translations.literal: His father Feizhi was a Staff Officer to the General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feizhi was a staff officer on the staff of the General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 家傳譜學。

translations.literal: The family handed down the study of genealogies.
translations.idiomatic: His family had a hereditary tradition of genealogical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武時，青州人發古塚，銘云：「青州世子，東海女郎。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowu's reign of Song, men of Qing province opened an ancient tomb; the inscription read: "Heir of Qing province, a maiden of Donghai."
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaowu of Song's reign, people in Qing province excavated an ancient tomb whose inscription ran: "Heir of Qing province, a maiden of Donghai."

sentences.zh: 」帝問學士鮑照、徐爰、蘇寶生，並不能悉。

translations.literal: " The emperor asked the academicians Bao Zhao, Xu Ai, and Su Baosheng, but none could explain it fully.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor questioned the scholars Bao Zhao, Xu Ai, and Su Baosheng, yet none could account for it completely.

sentences.zh: 希鏡對曰：「此是司馬越女嫁苟晞兒。

translations.literal: Xijing replied: "This is the daughter of Sima Yue married to the son of Gou Xi."
translations.idiomatic: Xijing answered: "This records the marriage of Sima Yue's daughter to Gou Xi's son."

sentences.zh: 」檢訪果然，由是見遇，敕希鏡注郭子。

translations.literal: " When the facts were checked, it proved so; from this he met with favor, and the emperor ordered Xijing to annotate the genealogy of the Guo clan.
translations.idiomatic: " When investigators verified the matter, it proved true. Thereafter he won imperial favor, and Xijing was ordered to annotate the genealogy of the Guo clan.

sentences.zh: 升明中，齊高帝嘉希鏡世學，取為驃騎參軍、武陵王國郎中令。

translations.literal: During the Shengming era, Emperor Gao of Qi admired Xijing's hereditary learning and took him as Staff Officer to the General of Agile Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Kingdom of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengming era, Emperor Gao of Qi admired Xijing's family tradition of scholarship and appointed him staff officer to the General of Agile Cavalry and palace attendant of the Kingdom of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 曆大司馬司徒府參軍。

translations.literal: He successively served as staff officer in the offices of the Grand Marshal and the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as a staff officer in the offices of the Grand Marshal and the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良使希鏡撰見客譜，出為句容令。

translations.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling had Xijing compile a register of visiting guests; he was then sent out as Magistrate of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling had Xijing compile a register of visiting guests, after which Xijing was posted as magistrate of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 先是，譜學未有名家，希鏡祖弼之廣集百氏譜記，專心習業。

translations.literal: Previously genealogy had no famous masters; Xijing's grandfather Bizhi widely gathered genealogical records of the hundred clans and devoted himself single-mindedly to the study.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, genealogical scholarship had no celebrated master; Xijing's grandfather Bizhi amassed genealogical records from countless clans and devoted himself entirely to the craft.

sentences.zh: 晉太元中，朝廷給弼之令史書吏，撰定繕寫，藏秘閣及左戶曹。

translations.literal: In the Taiyuan era of Jin, the court assigned Bizhi clerks and scribes to compile and copy them, storing them in the Secret Archive and the Left Households Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin Taiyuan era, the court supplied Bizhi with clerks and copyists to compile and transcribe the records, which were then stored in the Secret Archive and the Left Households Bureau.

sentences.zh: 希鏡三世傳學，凡十八州士族譜，合百帙，七百餘卷，該究精悉，皆如貫珠，當時莫比。

translations.literal: Xijing inherited the learning for three generations; genealogies of gentry clans from eighteen provinces totaled a hundred fascicles and more than seven hundred scrolls, exhaustive and precise, strung like pearls on a thread—unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing inherited this learning across three generations; his genealogies of noble clans from eighteen provinces filled a hundred fascicles and more than seven hundred scrolls—exhaustive, precise, and strung together like pearls on a cord, unmatched in his day.

sentences.zh: 永明中，衛將軍王儉抄次百家譜，與希鏡參懷撰定。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, General of the Guard Wang Jian collated the genealogies of the hundred clans and, together with Xijing, jointly planned and finalized them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era, General of the Guard Wang Jian collated the genealogies of the hundred clans and worked with Xijing to plan and finalize the compilation.

sentences.zh: 建武初，希鏡遷長水校尉，傖人王泰寶買襲琅邪譜，尚書令王晏以啟明帝，希鏡坐被收，當極法。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, Xijing was promoted to Colonel of the Long River; the northern immigrant Wang Taibao bought and usurped the Langya genealogy; Minister over the Masses Wang Yan reported this to Emperor Ming; Xijing was implicated, arrested, and faced the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianwu era, Xijing was promoted to Colonel of the Long River. When the northern immigrant Wang Taibao purchased and forged the Langya genealogy, Minister over the Masses Wang Yan reported the matter to Emperor Ming. Xijing was implicated, arrested, and condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 子棲長謝罪，稽顙流血，朝廷哀之，免希鏡罪。

translations.literal: His son Qi prostrated himself in long apology, knocking his brow until it bled; the court took pity and pardoned Xijing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi prostrated himself in prolonged apology, knocking his forehead to the ground until it bled; moved to pity, the court pardoned Xijing.

sentences.zh: 後為北中郎參軍，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as Staff Officer to the General of the North and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as staff officer to the General of the North and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 撰氏族要狀及人名書，並行于時。

translations.literal: He compiled Essential Records of Clans and a Book of Personal Names, both widely circulated at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essential Records of Clans and a Book of Personal Names, both of which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 袁峻字孝高，陳郡陽夏人，魏郎中令渙之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan Jun, styled Xiaogao, was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery and eighth-generation descendant of Huan, Director of the Masters of Writing under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jun, styled Xiaogao, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery and was the eighth-generation descendant of Huan, Director of the Masters of Writing under Wei.

sentences.zh: 早孤，篤志好學。

translations.literal: He lost his father early and devoted himself zealously to learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he pursued learning with fierce dedication.

sentences.zh: 家貧無書，每從人假借，必皆抄寫，自課日五十紙，紙數不登則不止。

translations.literal: Poor and without books at home, whenever he borrowed from others he always copied them out, setting himself fifty sheets a day and not stopping until the quota was met.
translations.idiomatic: His family was too poor to own books; whenever he borrowed one he copied it out in full, assigning himself fifty sheets a day and refusing to stop until the count was complete.

sentences.zh: 訥言語，工文辭。

translations.literal: Slow of speech, skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was slow of speech but accomplished in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝雅好辭賦，時獻文章于南闕者相望焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang greatly loved rhapsodies and poetry; at the time those presenting writings at the southern gate were unending.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang had a deep love of rhapsodies and fu poetry, and in those days the stream of writers presenting their work at the southern palace gate never ceased.

sentences.zh: 天監六年，峻乃擬揚雄官箴奏之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianjian, Jun modeled Yang Xiong's Admonitions for Officials and presented it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianjian, Jun modeled his submission on Yang Xiong's Admonitions for Officials and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉焉，賜束帛，除員外郎，散騎侍郎，直文德學士省，抄史記、漢書各為二十卷。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, granted him silks, appointed him Supernumerary Official and Attendant Cavalier, assigned him to the Academy at Wende, and had him abridge the Records of the Grand Historian and Book of Han into twenty scrolls each.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, granted him silks, and appointed him supernumerary official and attendant cavalier, assigning him to the Academy at Wende with orders to abridge the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han into twenty scrolls each.

sentences.zh: 又奉敕與陸倕各制新闕銘云。

translations.literal: He was further ordered, together with Lu Chui, each to compose an inscription for the new palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was further ordered, together with Lu Chui, each to compose an inscription for the new palace gate.

sentences.zh: 劉昭字宣卿，平原高唐人，晉太尉寔九世孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhao, styled Xuanqing, was from Gaotang in Pingyuan and ninth-generation descendant of Shi, Grand Commandant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao, styled Xuanqing, came from Gaotang in Pingyuan commandery and was the ninth-generation descendant of Shi, Grand Commandant of Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖伯龍，居父憂以孝聞，宋武帝敕皇太子諸王並往吊慰，官至少府卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bolong was famed for filial piety while mourning his father; Emperor Wu of Song ordered the Crown Prince and the princes all to go offer condolences; he rose to Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bolong won renown for filial devotion during his father's mourning; Emperor Wu of Song ordered the crown prince and all the princes to visit and offer condolences, and Bolong eventually rose to privy treasurer.

sentences.zh: 父彪，齊征虜晉安王記室。

translations.literal: His father Biao was secretary to the Prince of Jin'an on the staff of the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Biao served as secretary to the Prince of Jin'an under the General Who Pacifies the Barbarians during Qi.

sentences.zh: 昭幼清警，通老、莊義。

translations.literal: Zhao from youth was clear and quick, and versed in the teachings of Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhao was bright and alert, and he mastered the teachings of Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 及長，勤學善屬文，外兄江淹早相稱賞。

translations.literal: When grown, he studied diligently and was skilled at composition; his cousin Jiang Yan praised him early on.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he studied hard and wrote well; his cousin Jiang Yan praised him early.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，累遷中軍臨川王記室。

translations.literal: Under Liang in the Tianjian era, he was promoted repeatedly to secretary to the Prince of Linchuan on the staff of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang during the Tianjian era he rose in successive appointments to secretary to the Prince of Linchuan on the central army staff.

sentences.zh: 初，昭伯父肜集眾家晉書注干寶晉紀為四十卷，至昭集後漢同異以注范曄後漢，世稱博悉。

translations.literal: Initially Zhao's father's elder brother Tong gathered annotations to histories of Jin from various houses and annotated Gan Bao's Annals of Jin in forty scrolls; Zhao then gathered Later Han parallels and differences to annotate Fan Ye's Book of Later Han—called exhaustive by the world.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhao's father's elder brother Tong collected annotations from various houses to histories of Jin and annotated Gan Bao's Annals of Jin in forty scrolls; Zhao then gathered parallels and variants on the Later Han to annotate Fan Ye's Book of Later Han, work the age hailed as encyclopedic.

sentences.zh: 卒於剡令。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Magistrate of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as magistrate of Shan.

sentences.zh: 集注後漢一百三十卷，幼童傳一卷，文集十卷。

translations.literal: Collected annotations to the Later Han in one hundred thirty scrolls, one scroll of Biographies of Young Children, and ten scrolls of collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: His collected annotations to the Later Han ran to one hundred thirty scrolls; he also left one scroll of Biographies of Young Children and ten scrolls of collected writings.

sentences.zh: 子絛字言明，亦好學，通三禮，位尚書祠部郎，著先聖本記十卷行於世。

translations.literal: His son Tao, styled Yanming, also loved learning, mastered the Three Rites, served as Gentleman of the Ancestral Temple in the Ministry of Works, and wrote Ten Scrolls on the Origins of the Sage, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao, styled Yanming, also loved learning and mastered the Three Rites; he served as gentleman of the ancestral temple in the Ministry of Works and wrote Ten Scrolls on the Origins of the Sage, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 絛弟緩字含度，為湘東王中錄事。

translations.literal: Tao's younger brother Huan, styled Handu, was chief recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's younger brother Huan, styled Handu, served as chief recorder to the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 性虛遠，有氣調，風流疊宕，名高一府。

translations.literal: By nature withdrawn and lofty, with presence and bearing, elegant and unbounded in spirit, his renown topped the whole prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was aloof and far-seeing, with fine presence and bearing; elegant and free-spirited, his reputation stood above everyone in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 常云：「不須名位，所須衣食。

translations.literal: He often said: "I need no titles or rank; what I need is food and clothing."
translations.idiomatic: He often said: "I have no need of titles or rank—only food and clothing."

sentences.zh: 不用身後之譽，唯重目前知見。」

translations.literal: I do not want posthumous fame—only the regard of those who know me now."
translations.idiomatic: I care nothing for praise after death; I value only the esteem of those who know me in the present."

sentences.zh: 鍾嶸字仲偉，潁川長社人，晉侍中雅七世孫也。

translations.literal: Zhong Rong, styled Zhongwei, was from Changshe in Yingchuan and seventh-generation descendant of Ya, Palace Attendant of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Rong, styled Zhongwei, came from Changshe in Yingchuan commandery and was the seventh-generation descendant of Ya, palace attendant of Jin.

sentences.zh: 父蹈，齊中軍參軍。

translations.literal: His father Dao was a staff officer on the Central Army staff in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dao served as a staff officer on the central army staff during Qi.

sentences.zh: 嶸與兄岏、弟嶼並好學，有思理。

translations.literal: Rong, together with his elder brother Wan and younger brother Yu, all loved learning and possessed reflective insight.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, his elder brother Wan, and his younger brother Yu all loved learning and had thoughtful minds.

sentences.zh: 嶸齊永明中為國子生，明周易。

translations.literal: In Qi during Yongming, Rong was a student at the Imperial Academy and understood the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming in Qi, Rong was a student at the Imperial Academy and mastered the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍王儉領祭酒，頗賞接之。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Wang Jian served as Chancellor and greatly appreciated and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Wang Jian, serving as chancellor of the academy, took a strong liking to him and drew him close.

sentences.zh: 建武初，為南康王侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was Gentleman Attendant to the Prince of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jianwu era he served as gentleman attendant to the Prince of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 時齊明帝躬親細務，綱目亦密，於是郡縣及六署九府常行職事，莫不爭自啟聞，取決詔敕。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Ming of Qi personally attended to minute affairs and the net of governance was tight; thus in commanderies, counties, the six bureaus and nine offices, routine duties—none failed to compete in reporting upwards for decisions by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Ming of Qi personally handled minute affairs, and the web of administration was drawn tight; commanderies, counties, the six bureaus, and the nine offices all competed to report routine business upward and await decisions by imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 文武勳舊皆不歸選部，於是憑勢互相通進，人君之務，粗為繁密。

translations.literal: Civil and military merit-holders no longer fell under the Selection Bureau; relying on power they mutually recommended one another; the sovereign's duties had become roughly overwrought.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious civil and military officials no longer passed through the Selection Bureau; instead they used their influence to push one another forward, and the sovereign's business had grown roughly overburdened.

sentences.zh: 嶸乃上書言：「古者明君揆才頒政，量能授職，三公坐而論道，九卿作而成務，天子可恭己南面而已。

translations.literal: Rong then submitted a memorial saying: "In antiquity enlightened rulers measured talent to distribute governance, gauged capacity to assign office; the Three Dukes sat and discoursed on the Way, the Nine Ministers acted and completed their tasks—the Son of Heaven could reverently fold his hands and face south, that was all."
translations.idiomatic: Rong then submitted a memorial saying: "In antiquity enlightened rulers measured talent before distributing office, and matched ability to duty; the Three Dukes sat and discoursed on the Way while the Nine Ministers acted and completed their tasks—the Son of Heaven need only fold his hands in reverence and face south."

sentences.zh: 」書奏，上不懌，謂太中大夫顧暠曰：「鍾嶸何人，欲斷朕機務，卿識之不？

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was displeased and said to Grand Master of Palace Gu Mao: "Who is Zhong Rong, wishing to cut off my administrative work—do you know him?"
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor was displeased and said to Grand Master of Palace Gu Mao: "Who is this Zhong Rong who wants to cut me off from the business of state—do you know him?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「嶸雖位末名卑，而所言或有可采。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Though Rong's rank is low and his name obscure, what he says may have points worth adopting."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "Though Rong holds a low post and an obscure name, what he says may yet have points worth heeding."

sentences.zh: 且繁碎職事，各有司存，今人主總而親之，是人主愈勞而人臣愈逸，所謂代庖人宰而為大匠斲也。

translations.literal: Moreover, intricate duties each have their responsible offices; when the ruler gathers them all and handles them personally, the ruler grows ever more weary while ministers grow ever more idle—what is called the cook replacing the butcher and the master carpenter hewing wood himself."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, intricate duties each have their proper offices; when the ruler gathers them all and handles them personally, the ruler grows ever more weary while his ministers grow ever more idle—what is meant by the cook taking the butcher's place and the master carpenter doing the hewing himself."

sentences.zh: 」上不顧而他言。

translations.literal: " The emperor paid no heed and changed the subject.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor paid no attention and turned to other matters.

sentences.zh: 永元末，除司徒行參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan he was appointed Acting Staff Officer to the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongyuan era he was appointed acting staff officer to the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，制度雖革，而未能盡改前弊，嶸上言曰：「永元肇亂，坐弄天爵，勳非即戎，官以賄就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, though institutions were reformed, earlier abuses were not wholly corrected; Rong submitted a memorial saying: "Yongyuan's disorder began with idle wielding of heavenly ranks—merit came not from taking up arms, offices were obtained by bribery."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, though institutions had been reformed, the abuses of the past were not fully corrected; Rong submitted a memorial saying: "The Yongyuan disorders began when men idly traded in heavenly ranks—merit owed nothing to taking up arms, and office was bought with bribes."

sentences.zh: 揮一金而取九列，寄片劄以招六校。

translations.literal: A fistful of gold could win the ninth rank; a brief note could summon six colonelships.
translations.idiomatic: A handful of gold could buy the ninth rank; a brief note could secure six colonelships.

sentences.zh: 騎都塞市，郎將填街。

translations.literal: Commandants of cavalry choked the markets; general officers filled the streets.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry commandants clogged the markets, and general officers packed the streets.

sentences.zh: 服既纓組，尚為臧獲之事，職雖黃散，猶躬胥徒之役。

translations.literal: Though already wearing insignia of rank, they still performed servants' tasks; though holding lofty civil posts, they still personally did clerks' and laborers' drudgery.
translations.idiomatic: Though they already wore the insignia of office, they still did servants' work; though their posts were lofty civil appointments, they still performed clerks' and laborers' tasks in person.

sentences.zh: 名實淆紊，茲焉莫甚。

translations.literal: Names and realities were tangled—nowhere was the confusion graver.
translations.idiomatic: Names and realities were tangled beyond measure—nowhere was the disorder worse.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂永元諸軍官是素族士人，自有清貫，而因斯受爵，一宜削除，以懲澆競。

translations.literal: This subject humbly considers that the military officers of Yongyuan who were gentry of established clans already had their proper career tracks yet received enfeoffments through this—they should all be removed to punish reckless competition.
translations.idiomatic: This subject humbly holds that the military officers of Yongyuan who were gentry of established clans already had their proper career paths yet received titles through this abuse—all such titles should be struck to punish reckless ambition.

sentences.zh: 若吏姓寒人，聽極其門品，不當因軍遂濫清級。

translations.literal: If they were of clerical, low-born surname, let them reach only their clan's proper grade—they should not through military service overflow into exalted rank.
translations.idiomatic: If they were of low-born clerical families, let them rise only to their clan's proper grade—they should not through military service flood into exalted rank.

sentences.zh: 若僑雜傖楚，應在綏撫，正宜嚴斷祿力，絕其妨正，直乞虛號而已。

translations.literal: If they were mixed immigrant northerners, they belong under pacification—it is right to sever their salaries and stipends strictly, cut off their obstruction of proper governance, and grant only empty titles.
translations.idiomatic: If they were mixed bands of northern immigrants, they belong under pacification—it is right to cut off their salaries and stipends strictly, stop their interference with proper governance, and grant them empty titles and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」敕付尚書行之。

translations.literal: " An edict was issued entrusting it to the Ministry of Works for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict was issued entrusting the proposal to the Ministry of Works for implementation.

sentences.zh: 衡陽王元簡出守會稽，引為寧朔記室，專掌文翰。

translations.literal: When Prince Yuanjian of Hengyang went out to govern Kuaiji, he recruited Rong as secretary to the General Pacifying the North, exclusively in charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yuanjian of Hengyang went out to govern Kuaiji, he took Rong on as secretary to the General Pacifying the North, putting him solely in charge of literary work.

sentences.zh: 時居士何胤築室若邪山，山發洪水，漂拔樹石，此室獨存。

translations.literal: At the time the lay Buddhist He Yin built a dwelling on Mount Ruoye; the mountain sent down floods that swept away trees and stones, yet this dwelling alone survived.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the lay Buddhist He Yin built a dwelling on Mount Ruoye; when the mountain unleashed floods that swept away trees and stones, this dwelling alone remained standing.

sentences.zh: 元簡令嶸作瑞室頌以旌表之，辭甚典麗。

translations.literal: Yuan Jian had Rong compose an Eulogy for the Auspicious Chamber to honor it—the language was very classical and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jian had Rong compose an Eulogy for the Auspicious Chamber to honor the site; the language was richly classical and elegant.

sentences.zh: 遷西中郎晉安王記室。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secretary to the Prince of Jin'an on the Western Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to secretary to the Prince of Jin'an on the western army staff.

sentences.zh: 嶸嘗求譽于沈約，約拒之。

translations.literal: Rong once sought Shen Yue's praise; Yue refused him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong once sought praise from Shen Yue, but Yue refused him.

sentences.zh: 及約卒，嶸品古今詩為評，言其優劣，云：「觀休文眾制，五言最優。

translations.literal: When Yue died, Rong graded ancient and modern poetry in a critique, judging merits and defects, saying: "Surveying Xiuywen's many compositions, his five-character verse is finest."
translations.idiomatic: After Yue died, Rong graded ancient and modern poetry in his critique, judging strengths and weaknesses, and wrote: "Surveying Xiuywen's many compositions, his five-character verse is the finest."

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，相王愛文，王元長等皆宗附約。

translations.literal: In Qi during Yongming, the Prince of Jingling loved literature; Wang Yuanzhang and others all looked up to and attached themselves to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming in Qi, the Prince of Jingling loved literature, and Wang Yuanzhang and others all looked up to Yue and gathered around him.

sentences.zh: 于時謝朓未遒，江淹才盡，範雲名級又微，故稱獨步。

translations.literal: At the time Xie Tiao had not yet reached full force, Jiang Yan's talent was spent, Fan Yun's fame and rank were modest—thus Yue was called unrivaled.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xie Tiao had not yet reached full strength, Jiang Yan's talent was exhausted, and Fan Yun's reputation and rank were modest—so Yue was called unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 故當辭密于範，意淺于江」。

translations.literal: Therefore his diction should be tighter than Fan's, his meaning shallower than Jiang's."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly his diction is tighter than Fan Yun's, his meaning shallower than Jiang Yan's."

sentences.zh: 蓋追宿憾，以此報約也。

translations.literal: This was plainly settling an old grudge, returning the slight to Yue in this way.
translations.idiomatic: This was plainly settling an old grievance and repaying Yue in kind.

sentences.zh: 頃之卒官。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 岏字長丘，位建康令卒。

translations.literal: Wan, styled Changqiu, served as Magistrate of Jiankang and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, styled Changqiu, served as magistrate of Jiankang and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 著良吏傳十卷。

translations.literal: He wrote Ten Scrolls of Biographies of Good Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Ten Scrolls of Biographies of Good Officials.

sentences.zh: 嶼字季望，永嘉郡丞。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Jiwang, was Assistant Governor of Yongjia commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Jiwang, served as assistant governor of Yongjia commandery.

sentences.zh: 周興嗣字思纂，陳郡項人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Xingsi, styled Mizuan, was a native of Xiang in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xingsi, styled Mizuan, came from Xiang in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 世居姑孰，博學善屬文。

translations.literal: For generations his family lived at Gushu; he was broadly learned and skilled in composition.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived at Gushu; he was broadly learned and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 嘗步自姑孰，投宿逆旅，夜有人謂曰：「子才學邁世，初當見識貴臣，卒被知英主。

translations.literal: Once walking from Gushu, he lodged at an inn; at night someone said to him: "Your talent and learning surpass the age—you will first be noticed by eminent ministers and in the end known by a heroic sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Once, walking out from Gushu, he lodged at a roadside inn; in the night someone said to him: "Your talent and learning surpass your age—you will first be recognized by eminent ministers and in the end be known by a heroic sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」言終不測所之。

translations.literal: " When the words ended, no one could tell where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: " When the words ended, no one could tell where the speaker had gone.

sentences.zh: 齊隆昌中，侍郎謝朏為吳興太守，唯與興嗣初談文史而已。

translations.literal: In Longchang of Qi, Gentleman Attendant Xie Tiao was Governor of Wuxing and spoke with Xingsi about history and literature on first acquaintance only.
translations.idiomatic: During Longchang in Qi, Gentleman Attendant Xie Tiao served as governor of Wuxing and, on first meeting Xingsi, spoke with him only about history and literature.

sentences.zh: 及罷郡，因大相談薦。

translations.literal: When he left the commandery, he strongly recommended him in conversation.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the commandery, he spoke at length in recommendation of him.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，奏休平賦，其文甚美，武帝嘉之，拜安成王國侍郎，直華林省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, he submitted the Rhapsody on Rest and Peace; its prose was very fine; Emperor Wu was pleased, appointed him Gentleman of the Kingdom of Ancheng, serving at Hualin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, he submitted the Rhapsody on Rest and Peace; its prose was exquisite, and Emperor Wu was pleased. He appointed Xingsi gentleman of the Kingdom of Ancheng and assigned him to serve at Hualin.

sentences.zh: 其年，河南獻舞馬，詔興嗣與待詔到沆、張率為賦，帝以興嗣為工，擢拜員外散騎侍郎，進直文德、壽光省。

translations.literal: That year Henan presented dancing horses; the emperor ordered Xingsi together with Awaiting-Edict Dao Hang and Zhang Shuai to compose rhapsodies; judging Xingsi's the finest, he promoted him to Supernumerary Attendant Cavalier and advanced him to serve at Wende and Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Henan presented dancing horses; the emperor ordered Xingsi, together with awaiting-edict Dao Hang and Zhang Shuai, to compose rhapsodies. Judging Xingsi's the finest, he promoted him to supernumerary attendant cavalier and advanced him to serve at Wende and Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 時武帝以三橋舊宅為光宅寺，敕興嗣與陸倕各制寺碑，及成俱奏，帝用興嗣所制。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor converted his old Three Bridges residence into Guangzhe Temple, ordered Xingsi and Lu Chui each to compose a temple stele; when both were finished and submitted, the emperor used Xingsi's.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor converted his old Three Bridges residence into Guangzhe Temple and ordered Xingsi and Lu Chui each to compose a temple stele; when both were finished and submitted, the emperor chose Xingsi's.

sentences.zh: 自是銅表銘、柵塘碣、檄魏文、次韻王羲之書千字，並使興嗣為文。

translations.literal: From then on, inscriptions for bronze pillars, steles for palisade ponds, proclamations to Wei, and the Thousand-Character Text arranged after Wang Xizhi's calligraphy—all were entrusted to Xingsi for composition.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, inscriptions for bronze pillars, steles for palisade ponds, proclamations to Wei, and the Thousand-Character Text arranged after Wang Xizhi's calligraphy were all entrusted to Xingsi.

sentences.zh: 每奏，帝稱善，賜金帛。

translations.literal: Whenever he submitted, the emperor praised his work and granted gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he submitted a piece, the emperor praised it and granted him gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 後佐撰國史。

translations.literal: Later he assisted in compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Later he assisted in compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 興嗣兩手先患風疽，十二年，又染癘疾，左目盲。

translations.literal: Xingsi first suffered wind-sores on both hands for twelve years, then contracted leprosy and went blind in the left eye.
translations.idiomatic: Xingsi had first suffered wind-sores on both hands for twelve years; he then contracted leprosy and lost sight in his left eye.

sentences.zh: 帝撫其手，嗟曰：「斯人而有斯疾。

translations.literal: The emperor stroked his hand and sighed: "Such a man—yet such affliction."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stroked his hand and sighed: "That such a man should have such an affliction."

sentences.zh: 」手疏疽方以賜之。

translations.literal: " He personally wrote out a prescription for sores and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: " He personally wrote out a prescription for sores and bestowed it upon him.

sentences.zh: 任昉又愛其才，常曰：「興嗣若無此疾，旬日當至御史中丞。

translations.literal: Ren Fang also admired his talent and often said: "If Xingsi did not have this illness, within ten days he would reach Censor-in-Chief."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang also admired his talent and often said: "If Xingsi did not suffer this illness, within ten days he would reach censor-in-chief."

sentences.zh: 」十七年，為給事中，直西省。

translations.literal: " In the seventeenth year he was made Attendant Within the Palace Gates, serving in the Western Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " In the seventeenth year he was appointed attendant within the palace gates and assigned to the Western Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周舍奉敕注武帝所制歷代賦，啟興嗣與焉。

translations.literal: Zhou She, by imperial order annotating the successive dynasties' rhapsodies composed by Emperor Wu, included Xingsi in the work.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order Zhou She annotated the rhapsodies on successive dynasties composed by Emperor Wu and included Xingsi in the project.

sentences.zh: 普通二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Putong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Putong.

sentences.zh: 所撰皇帝實錄、皇德記、起居注、職儀等百餘卷，文集十卷。

translations.literal: Works he compiled included the Veritable Records of the Emperor, Record of Imperial Virtue, Diurnal Records, Regulations of Office, and more than a hundred scrolls in all, plus ten scrolls of collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included the Veritable Records of the Emperor, Record of Imperial Virtue, Diurnal Records, Regulations of Office, and more than a hundred scrolls in all, as well as ten scrolls of collected works.

sentences.zh: 吳均字叔庠，吳興故鄣人也。

translations.literal: Wu Jun, styled Shuxiang, was a native of Gucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jun, styled Shuxiang, came from Gucheng in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世寒賤，至均好學有俊才，沈約嘗見均文，頗相稱賞。

translations.literal: His family background was poor and lowly; as for Jun himself, he loved learning and had outstanding talent; Shen Yue once saw Jun's writings and praised them highly.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and lowly, but Jun himself loved learning and had outstanding talent; Shen Yue once read Jun's writings and praised them warmly.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，柳惲為吳興，召補主簿，日引與賦詩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, Liu Yun governed Wuxing, summoned him as chief clerk, and daily invited him to compose poetry together.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang, when Liu Yun governed Wuxing, he summoned Jun as chief clerk and daily invited him to compose poetry together.

sentences.zh: 均文體清拔，有古氣，好事者或學之，謂為「吳均體」。

translations.literal: Jun's literary style was clear and striking, with an antique flavor; enthusiasts sometimes imitated it, calling it the "Wu Jun style."
translations.idiomatic: Jun's literary style was clear and striking, with an antique flavor; enthusiasts sometimes imitated it and called it the "Wu Jun style."

sentences.zh: 均嘗不得意，贈惲詩而去，久之復來，惲遇之如故，弗之憾也。

translations.literal: Jun once, discontented, presented Liu with a poem and left; after a long while he returned; Liu received him as before, bearing no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once, discontented, Jun presented Liu with a parting poem and left; long afterward he returned, and Liu received him as before, without the least resentment.

sentences.zh: 薦之臨川靖惠王，王稱之于武帝，即日召入賦詩，悅焉。

translations.literal: He recommended him to Prince Jinghui of Linchuan; the prince praised him to Emperor Wu, who that same day summoned him to compose poetry and was delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu recommended him to Prince Jinghui of Linchuan; the prince praised him to Emperor Wu, who summoned him that same day to compose poetry and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 待詔著作，累遷奉朝請。

translations.literal: He served as Drafting Attendant in the Directorate of Compilations and was repeatedly promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Drafting Attendant in the Directorate of Compilations and was eventually promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 先是，均將著史以自名，欲撰齊書，求借齊起居注及群臣行狀，武帝不許，遂私撰齊春秋奏之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jun intended to make a name for himself by compiling history; he wished to write a History of Qi, and asked to borrow the Qi diurnal records and the biographical affidavits of the various ministers, but Emperor Wu did not permit it; he then privately compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals of Qi and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jun had hoped to win lasting fame by writing history. Wishing to compile a History of Qi, he asked to borrow the Qi court diurnal records and the biographical affidavits of ministers, but Emperor Wu refused. Jun then privately wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals of Qi and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 書稱帝為齊明帝佐命，帝惡其實錄，以其書不實，使中書舍人劉之遴詰問數十條，竟支離無對。

translations.literal: The book called the emperor one who had aided in establishing Emperor Ming of Qi; the emperor hated its truthful record, and on the grounds that the book was untrue had the Secretariat Gentleman Liu Zhiliao question him on several dozen points; in the end his answers were fragmented and he could not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The book described the emperor as a man who had helped establish Emperor Ming of Qi. The emperor resented this truthful account and, claiming the work was inaccurate, had Secretariat Gentleman Liu Zhiliao cross-examine him on dozens of points. In the end his replies were incoherent and he could not answer.

sentences.zh: 敕付省焚之，坐免職。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it handed to the provincial office to be burned, and he was dismissed from office as punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the work sent to the provincial offices to be burned, and he was dismissed from his post.

sentences.zh: 尋有敕召見，使撰通史，起三皇訖齊代。

translations.literal: Soon afterward an edict summoned him for an audience and ordered him to compile a comprehensive history from the Three Sovereigns down through the Qi dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict summoned him to court and charged him with compiling a comprehensive history from the Three Sovereigns through the Qi dynasty.

sentences.zh: 均草本紀、世家已畢，唯列傳未就，卒。

translations.literal: Jun's draft basic annals and noble-house accounts were finished, but only the biographies were not completed when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had finished draft basic annals and accounts of noble houses, but the biographies were still unfinished when he died.

sentences.zh: 均注范曄後漢書九十卷，著齊春秋三十卷，廟記十卷，十二州記十六卷，錢唐先賢傳五卷，續文釋五卷，文集二十卷。

translations.literal: Jun annotated Fan Ye's Book of Later Han in ninety scrolls, and wrote the Spring and Autumn Annals of Qi in thirty scrolls, Record of Temples in ten scrolls, Record of the Twelve Provinces in sixteen scrolls, Biographies of Worthies of Qiantang in five scrolls, Continued Literary Exegesis in five scrolls, and collected writings in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Jun annotated Fan Ye's Book of Later Han in ninety scrolls and authored the Spring and Autumn Annals of Qi in thirty scrolls, Record of Temples in ten scrolls, Record of the Twelve Provinces in sixteen scrolls, Biographies of Worthies of Qiantang in five scrolls, Continued Literary Exegesis in five scrolls, and a collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 先是有濟陽江洪，工屬文，為建陽令，坐事死。

translations.literal: Before this there was Jiang Hong of Jiyang, skilled at literary composition, who served as magistrate of Jianyang and was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been Jiang Hong of Jiyang, a skilled writer who served as magistrate of Jianyang and was executed for a crime.

sentences.zh: 劉勰字彥和，東莞莒人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xie, styled Yanhe, was a native of Ju in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xie, styled Yanhe, came from Ju in Dongguan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父尚，越騎校尉。

translations.literal: His father Shang was Commandant of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shang served as Commandant of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 勰早孤，篤志好學。

translations.literal: Xie lost his father early and devoted himself wholeheartedly to learning.
translations.idiomatic: Xie lost his father early and devoted himself wholeheartedly to study.

sentences.zh: 家貧不婚娶，依沙門僧佑居，遂博通經論，因區別部類，錄而序之。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he did not marry; he lived with the monk Sengyou, and so came to master Buddhist sutras and treatises; he then distinguished their categories, recorded them, and arranged them in order.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to marry, he lived with the monk Sengyou, mastered Buddhist sutras and treatises, classified them by category, and compiled an ordered catalogue.

sentences.zh: 定林寺經藏，勰所定也。

translations.literal: The sutra repository of Dinglin Monastery was the one Xie organized.
translations.idiomatic: The sutra repository at Dinglin Monastery was organized by Xie.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，兼東宮通事舍人，時七廟饗薦已用蔬果，而二郊農社猶有犧牲，勰乃表言二郊宜與七廟同改。

translations.literal: During Tianjian under Liang, he concurrently served as Eastern Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs; at the time offerings at the seven ancestral temples already used fruits and vegetables, but the two suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the agricultural and soil-god rites still used sacrificial animals; Xie then submitted a memorial saying the two suburban sacrifices ought to be changed in the same way as the seven temples.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianjian under Liang, while serving concurrently as Eastern Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs, he noted that offerings at the seven ancestral temples already used fruits and vegetables, whereas the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the rites to the agricultural and soil gods still employed sacrificial animals. Xie submitted a memorial arguing that the suburban rites should be reformed to match the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書議，依勰所陳。

translations.literal: An edict referred the matter to the Secretariat for deliberation, and they followed what Xie had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the Secretariat for deliberation, and they adopted Xie's proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷步兵校尉，兼舍人如故，深被昭明太子愛接。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Infantry Commandant, and his concurrent service as Attendant remained as before; he was deeply favored and received by Crown Prince Zhaoming.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Infantry Commandant while continuing as Attendant as before, and was warmly favored by Crown Prince Zhaoming.

sentences.zh: 初，勰撰文心雕龍五十篇，論古今文體，其序略云：「予齒在逾立，嘗夜夢執丹漆之禮器，隨仲尼而南行，寤而喜曰：大哉，聖人之難見也，乃小子之垂夢歟！

translations.literal: At first Xie wrote The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons in fifty chapters, discussing literary forms ancient and modern; its preface in brief says: "When my years had passed thirty, I once dreamed at night that I held vermilion-lacquered ritual vessels and followed Zhongni southward; waking, I rejoiced and said: How great it is that the sage is hard to meet—could this be a dream granted to one so small as I!"
translations.idiomatic: At first Xie wrote The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons in fifty chapters, discussing literary forms ancient and modern. Its preface in brief says: "When I had passed thirty, I once dreamed at night that I held vermilion-lacquered ritual vessels and followed Confucius southward. On waking I rejoiced and said: How great it is that the sage is so hard to meet—could such a dream have been granted to one as insignificant as I?"

sentences.zh: 自生靈以來，未有如夫子者也。

translations.literal: Since living beings arose, there has never been anyone like the Master.
translations.idiomatic: Since living beings first arose, there has never been anyone like the Master.

sentences.zh: 敷贊聖旨，莫若注經，而馬、鄭諸儒弘之已精，就有深解，未足立家。

translations.literal: To spread and praise the sage's intent, nothing is better than annotating the classics; yet the various Ru such as Ma and Zheng have already developed them to refinement—even with deep understanding, that is not enough to establish one's own school.
translations.idiomatic: To spread and praise the sage's intent, nothing surpasses annotating the classics; yet scholars such as Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan have already refined that work to perfection—even profound understanding there would not suffice to establish one's own school.

sentences.zh: 唯文章之用，實經典枝條，五禮資之以成，六典因之致用。

translations.literal: Only the function of literature is truly a branch of the classics: the Five Rites rely on it to be completed, and the Six Canons employ it to achieve use.
translations.idiomatic: Only literature is truly a branch of the classics—the Five Rites depend on it for completion, and the Six Canons draw on it for practical use.

sentences.zh: 於是搦筆和墨，乃始論文。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took up the brush and mixed ink, and only then began to discourse on literature.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he took up brush and ink and began to write on literature.

sentences.zh: 其為文用四十九篇而已。

translations.literal: What he wrote on the function of literature amounted to forty-nine chapters, and no more.
translations.idiomatic: His discussion of the function of literature ran to forty-nine chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 」既成，未為時流所稱。

translations.literal: When it was finished, it was not praised by the leading men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, it won no praise from the leading writers of the day.

sentences.zh: 勰欲取定于沈約，無由自達，乃負書候約于車前，狀若貨鬻者。

translations.literal: Xie wished to obtain Shen Yue's judgment, but had no means to reach him on his own; he therefore carried the book and waited for Yue in front of his carriage, looking like a peddler selling goods.
translations.idiomatic: Xie wanted Shen Yue's judgment but had no way to reach him, so he carried the book and waited for Yue beside his carriage, looking like a street vendor.

sentences.zh: 約取讀，大重之，謂深得文理，常陳諸几案。

translations.literal: Yue took it and read it, greatly valued it, said it deeply grasped literary principle, and regularly kept it displayed on his desk.
translations.idiomatic: Yue took it, read it, and valued it highly, declaring that it deeply grasped literary principle; he kept it on his desk at all times.

sentences.zh: 勰為文長於佛理，都下寺塔及名僧碑誌，必請勰制文。

translations.literal: Xie was skilled in writing on Buddhist doctrine; for monasteries and pagodas in the capital and for steles and epitaphs of eminent monks, they invariably asked Xie to compose the texts.
translations.idiomatic: Xie excelled at writing on Buddhist doctrine; for temples and pagodas in the capital and for steles and epitaphs of eminent monks, he was invariably asked to compose the texts.

sentences.zh: 敕與慧震沙門于定林寺撰經證。

translations.literal: By edict he was paired with the monk Huizhen at Dinglin Monastery to compile sutra verification.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he joined the monk Huizhen at Dinglin Monastery to compile sutra collations.

sentences.zh: 功畢，遂求出家，先燔鬚髮自誓，敕許之。

translations.literal: When the work was finished, he then sought to leave the household life; first he burned his beard and hair as a vow, and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, he sought to become a monk, first burning his beard and hair as a vow; an edict granted permission.

sentences.zh: 乃變服改名慧地云。

translations.literal: He then changed his garb and renamed himself Huidi.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his garb and took the monastic name Huidi.

sentences.zh: 何思澄字元靜，東海郯人也。

translations.literal: He Sicheng, styled Yuanjing, was a native of Tan in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He Sicheng, styled Yuanjing, came from Tan in Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 父敬叔，齊長城令，有能名。

translations.literal: His father Jingshu was magistrate of Changcheng under Qi and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingshu served as magistrate of Changcheng under Qi and enjoyed a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 在縣清廉，不受禮遺，夏節至，忽牓門受餉，數日中得米二千餘斛，他物稱是，悉以代貧人輸租。

translations.literal: While in the county he was incorrupt and accepted no gifts; when the summer festival arrived, he suddenly posted a notice at the gate accepting offerings, and within several days received more than two thousand bushels of rice, with other goods in proportion, all of which he used to pay rent on behalf of the poor.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate he was incorruptible and accepted no gifts. When the summer festival arrived, he suddenly posted a notice at the gate inviting offerings; within a few days he received more than two thousand bushels of rice and comparable quantities of other goods, all of which he used to pay taxes on behalf of the poor.

sentences.zh: 思澄少勤學工文，為遊廬山詩，沈約見之，大相稱賞，自以為弗逮。

translations.literal: Sicheng from youth studied diligently and was skilled at writing; he composed a poem on traveling to Mount Lu; Shen Yue saw it and praised it greatly, considering himself not equal to it.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng studied diligently from youth and was skilled at writing. He composed a poem on traveling to Mount Lu; Shen Yue read it and praised it warmly, declaring himself unable to match it.

sentences.zh: 約郊居宅新構閣齋，因命工書人題此詩於壁。

translations.literal: Yue's suburban residence had a newly built pavilion study, and he therefore had a scribe inscribe this poem on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had just built a pavilion study at his suburban residence and had a scribe inscribe the poem on its wall.

sentences.zh: 傅昭嘗請思澄制釋奠詩，辭文典麗。

translations.literal: Fu Zhao once asked Sicheng to compose a poem for the Confucian sacrifice, and its language was classic and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhao once asked Sicheng to compose a poem for the Confucian sacrifice; the text was classic and elegant.

sentences.zh: 天監十五年，敕太子詹事徐勉舉學士入華林撰遍略，勉舉思澄、顧協、劉杳、王子雲、鍾嶼等五人以應選。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered the Crown Prince's Household Administrator Xu Mian to recommend scholars to enter Hualin to compile the Comprehensive Digest; Mian recommended Sicheng, Gu Xie, Liu Yao, Wang Ziyun, and Zhong Yu—five men in all—to answer the selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tianjian, an edict ordered Crown Prince's Household Administrator Xu Mian to recommend scholars to compile the Comprehensive Digest at Hualin. Mian recommended five men—Sicheng, Gu Xie, Liu Yao, Wang Ziyun, and Zhong Yu—for the task.

sentences.zh: 八年乃書成，合七百卷。

translations.literal: After eight years the book was completed, totaling seven hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years later the work was finished, totaling seven hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 思澄重交結，分書與諸賓朋校定，而終日造謁。

translations.literal: Sicheng valued social connections; he distributed copies to various guest-friends for proofreading, yet spent the whole day paying calls.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng valued social connections. He distributed copies to friends for proofreading, yet spent his days calling on acquaintances.

sentences.zh: 每宿昔作名一束，曉便命駕，朝賢無不悉狎，狎處即命食。

translations.literal: Each evening he prepared a bundle of names, and at dawn would order his carriage; there was no court worthy he did not know intimately, and wherever he was intimate he would order a meal.
translations.idiomatic: Each evening he prepared a list of names, and at dawn would set out in his carriage. There was scarcely a court official he did not know well, and wherever he called he would be served a meal.

sentences.zh: 有人方之樓護，欣然當之。

translations.literal: Some compared him to Lou Hu, and he gladly accepted the likeness.
translations.idiomatic: When someone compared him to Lou Hu, the great host of Han, he accepted the comparison with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 投晚還家，所齎名必盡。

translations.literal: Returning home toward evening, the names he had carried were always exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned home in the evening, every name on his list had been visited.

sentences.zh: 自廷尉正遷書侍御史。

translations.literal: From Director of the Court of Justice he was transferred to Supervising Censor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from Director of the Court of Justice to Supervising Censor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊以來，此職甚輕，天監初始重其選。

translations.literal: From Song and Qi onward this office had been very lightly regarded; only at the beginning of Tianjian was its selection first made weighty.
translations.idiomatic: From Song and Qi onward this office had carried little weight; only at the beginning of Tianjian was its selection taken seriously.

sentences.zh: 車前依尚書二丞給三騶，執盛印青囊，舊事糾彈官印綬在前故也。

translations.literal: Before his carriage, according to the two assistant directors of the Secretariat, three outriders were provided; he carried the seal case in a green pouch—an old custom because the censor's seal and sash came first.
translations.idiomatic: Before his carriage, following the precedent set for the two assistant directors of the Secretariat, three outriders were provided, and he carried the seal case in a green pouch—an old custom because the censor's seal and sash took precedence.

sentences.zh: 後除安西湘東王錄事參軍，兼東宮通事舍人。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Recorder under Prince Xiangdong, General Who Pacifies the West, and concurrently served as Eastern Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Recorder under Prince Xiangdong, General Who Pacifies the West, while continuing concurrently as Eastern Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時徐勉、周舍以才具當朝，並好思澄學，常遞日招致之。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Mian and Zhou She, both talented and holding power at court, alike admired Sicheng's learning and regularly invited him on alternate days.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Mian and Zhou She, both talented men holding power at court, admired Sicheng's learning and took turns inviting him day after day.

sentences.zh: 後卒于宣惠武陵王中錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Senior Recorder under Prince Wuling, General Who Proclaims Grace.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Senior Recorder under Prince Wuling, General Who Proclaims Grace.

sentences.zh: 文集十五卷。

translations.literal: Collected writings in fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to fifteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 初，思澄與宗人遜及子朗俱擅文名，時人語曰：「東海三何，子朗最多。

translations.literal: At first Sicheng, his clansman Xun, and Zilang were all famed for writing; people of the time said: "Among the Three He of Donghai, Zilang has the most."
translations.idiomatic: At first Sicheng, his clansman Xun, and Zilang were all renowned for their writing. People of the time said: "Among the Three He of Donghai, Zilang has the most."

sentences.zh: 」思澄聞之曰：「此言誤耳。

translations.literal: When Sicheng heard this he said: "This remark is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Sicheng heard this he said: "That remark is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，故當歸遜。

translations.literal: If it were not so, then the credit ought to go to Xun."
translations.idiomatic: If it were not so, the credit ought to go to Xun."

sentences.zh: 」思澄意謂宜在己也。

translations.literal: Sicheng's meaning was that it ought to be himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng in fact meant that the credit ought to be his.

sentences.zh: 子朗字世明，早有才思。

translations.literal: Zilang, styled Shiming, early showed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zilang, styled Shiming, showed literary talent from an early age.

sentences.zh: 周舍每與談，服其精理。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhou She conversed with him, he admired his refined reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhou She conversed with him, he admired the subtlety of his thought.

sentences.zh: 嘗為敗塚賦，擬莊周馬棰，其文甚工。

translations.literal: He once wrote a fu on a ruined mound, modeled on Zhuang Zhou's Horse Whip, and the text was very accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a fu on a ruined mound, modeled on Zhuang Zhou's Horse Whip, and the piece was highly accomplished.

sentences.zh: 世人語曰：「人中爽爽有子朗。

translations.literal: People of the world said: "Among men, bright and outstanding is Zilang."
translations.idiomatic: People said: "Among men, bright and outstanding stands Zilang."

sentences.zh: 」卒于國山令，年二十四。

translations.literal: He died while serving as magistrate of Guoshan, at the age of twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as magistrate of Guoshan, at the age of twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 王子雲，太原人，及江夏費昶，並為閭里才子。

translations.literal: Wang Ziyun, a man of Taiyuan, and Fei Chang of Jiangxia were both local literary talents.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ziyun of Taiyuan and Fei Chang of Jiangxia were both local literary talents.

sentences.zh: 昶善為樂府，又作鼓吹曲。

translations.literal: Chang was skilled at yuefu poetry and also composed martial procession songs.
translations.idiomatic: Chang excelled at yuefu poetry and also composed martial procession songs.

sentences.zh: 武帝重之，敕曰：「才意新拔，有足嘉異。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu valued him and issued an edict saying: "His talent and conception are fresh and striking, and worthy of special praise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu valued him and issued an edict saying: "Your talent and conception are fresh and striking, and worthy of special praise.

sentences.zh: 昔郎惲博物，卞蘭巧辭。

translations.literal: In former times Lang Yun was broadly learned and Bian Lan was artful in phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Lang Yun was broadly learned and Bian Lan was artful in phrasing.

sentences.zh: 束帛之賜，實惟勸善。

translations.literal: The gift of silks is truly meant to encourage excellence.
translations.idiomatic: The gift of silks is truly meant to encourage excellence.

sentences.zh: 可賜絹十匹。

translations.literal: He may be granted ten bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: Let ten bolts of silk be granted."

sentences.zh: 」子雲嘗為自吊文，甚美。

translations.literal: Ziyun once wrote a self-lament, which was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun once wrote a self-lament that was very fine.

sentences.zh: 任孝恭字孝恭，臨淮人也。

translations.literal: Ren Xiaogong, styled Xiaogong, was a native of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Xiaogong, styled Xiaogong, came from Linhuai commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖農夫，宋南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Nongfu was Governor of Southern Yu Province under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Nongfu served as Governor of Southern Yu Province under Song.

sentences.zh: 農夫弟候伯，位輔國將軍、行湘州事，並任將帥。

translations.literal: Nongfu's younger brother Houbo held the rank of General Who Assists the State and acted as administrator of Xiang Province; both served as generals.
translations.idiomatic: Nongfu's younger brother Houbo served as General Who Assists the State and acting administrator of Xiang Province; both men were military commanders.

sentences.zh: 孝恭幼孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xiaogong lost his father early and was known for serving his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong lost his father early and was known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 精力勤學，家貧無書，常崎嶇從人假借，每讀一遍，諷誦略無所遺。

translations.literal: With tireless energy he studied diligently; his family was poor and had no books, so he often went over rough paths to borrow from others, and each time he read a text once he could recite it from memory with scarcely anything forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with tireless energy. Too poor to own books, he often trudged over rough paths to borrow them, and after reading a text once he could recite it from memory with scarcely a word forgotten.

sentences.zh: 外祖丘它與武帝有舊，帝聞其有才學，召入西省撰史。

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Qiu Ta had old ties with Emperor Wu; the emperor heard that he had talent and learning and summoned him to the Western Secretariat to compile history.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather Qiu Ta had old ties with Emperor Wu. When the emperor heard of his talent and learning, he summoned him to the Western Secretariat to compile history.

sentences.zh: 初為奉朝請，進直壽光省，為司文侍郎，俄兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: At first he served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, then entered duty at the Shouguang Office as Vice Director for Documents, and soon concurrently served as Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, then entered duty at the Shouguang Office as Vice Director for Documents, and soon concurrently served as Secretariat Attendant-in-Ordinary for General Affairs.

sentences.zh: 敕遣制建陵寺刹下銘，又啟撰武帝集序文，並富麗。

translations.literal: By edict he was ordered to compose the inscription beneath the pagoda at Jianling Monastery, and he also submitted a preface for Emperor Wu's collected writings; both were rich and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he composed the inscription beneath the pagoda at Jianling Monastery and also submitted a preface for Emperor Wu's collected writings; both were rich and splendid.

sentences.zh: 自是專掌公家筆翰。

translations.literal: From then on he exclusively managed the brushwork of the public offices.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was put in charge of official documents.

sentences.zh: 孝恭為文敏速，若不留思，每奏稱善，累賜金帛。

translations.literal: Xiaogong wrote with quick facility, as if without lingering thought; each memorial was praised as good, and he was repeatedly granted gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong wrote with quick facility, as if without effort; each memorial won praise, and he was repeatedly rewarded with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 少從蕭寺雲法師讀經論，明佛理，至是蔬食持戒，信受甚篤。

translations.literal: From youth he studied sutras and treatises under Master Yun of Xiao Monastery, understood Buddhist doctrine, and by this time ate vegetables and kept the precepts, his faith and acceptance very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had studied sutras and treatises under Master Yun of Xiao Monastery and understood Buddhist doctrine; by this time he ate only vegetables, kept the precepts, and practiced his faith with deep devotion.

sentences.zh: 而性頗自伐，以才能尚人，於流輩中多有忽略，世以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he rather boasted of himself, looked down on others by reason of talent and ability, and among his peers often slighted many; the world for this thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was inclined to boast of his abilities and look down on others; among his peers he often slighted people, and for this the world thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，侯景寇逼，孝恭啟募兵，隸蕭正德。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing pressed in with invasion; Xiaogong submitted a request to raise troops and was attached to Xiao Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing, when Hou Jing pressed the capital, Xiaogong petitioned to raise troops and was placed under Xiao Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 正德入賊，孝恭還赴台，台門閉，侯景獲之，使作檄。

translations.literal: Zhengde went over to the rebels; Xiaogong returned to rush to the capital platform, but the platform gates were closed; Hou Jing seized him and made him compose a proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengde defected to the rebels, Xiaogong hurried back to the capital, but the palace gates were closed; Hou Jing seized him and forced him to compose a proclamation.

sentences.zh: 求還私第檢討，景許之，因走入東府。

translations.literal: He asked to return to his private residence to revise the draft; Jing permitted it, and he therefore fled into the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return home to revise the draft; Jing agreed, and he fled into the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 城陷，景斬銼之。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Jing executed him by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Hou Jing had him executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 協幼孤，養于舅氏。

translations.literal: Xie lost his father early and was raised by his uncle's family.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Xie lost his father early and was raised by his uncle's family.

sentences.zh: 少以器局稱。

translations.literal: From youth he was praised for breadth of character.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was praised for breadth of character and bearing.

sentences.zh: 博涉群書，工於草隸飛白。

translations.literal: He broadly mastered many books and was skilled in cursive, clerical, and feibai scripts.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and was skilled in cursive, clerical, and feibai calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 時吳人範懷約能隸書，協學其書，殆過真也。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Huaiyue of Wu could write clerical script; Xie studied his writing and nearly surpassed the original.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Fan Huaiyue of Wu was a master of clerical script; Xie studied his hand and nearly surpassed the original.

sentences.zh: 荊楚碑碣皆協所書。

translations.literal: The steles and tablets of Jing and Chu were all written by Xie.
translations.idiomatic: The steles and tablets throughout Jing and Chu were all written by Xie.

sentences.zh: 時又有會稽謝善勳能為八體六文，方寸千言，京兆韋仲善飛白，並在湘東王府。

translations.literal: At the time there were also Xie Shanxun of Kuaiji, who could write the eight script styles and six characters per square inch with a thousand characters per foot, and Wei Zhong of Jingzhao, skilled at feibai; both were in Prince Xiangdong's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xie Shanxun of Kuaiji, who could write in eight script styles and fit a thousand characters within a square inch, and Wei Zhong of Jingzhao, skilled at feibai, were also in Prince Xiangdong's establishment.

sentences.zh: 善勳為錄事參軍，仲為中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Shanxun served as Recorder and Zhong as Central Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxun served as Recorder and Zhong as Central Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 府中以協優於韋仲而減於善勳。

translations.literal: In the prince's establishment Xie was ranked above Wei Zhong but below Shanxun.
translations.idiomatic: In the prince's establishment Xie was ranked above Wei Zhong but below Shanxun.

sentences.zh: 善勳飲酒至數斗，醉後輒張眼大罵，雖復貴賤親疏無所擇也，時謂之謝方眼。

translations.literal: Shanxun would drink up to several dou of wine; when drunk he would open his eyes wide and curse loudly, sparing neither high nor low, near nor distant; people of the time called him Square-Eyed Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxun could drink several dou of wine at a sitting; when drunk he would stare wide-eyed and curse loudly, sparing no one whether high or low, friend or stranger. People of the time called him Square-Eyed Xie.

sentences.zh: 而胸衿夷坦，有士君子之操焉。

translations.literal: Yet his breast was open and level, and he had the conduct of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his heart was open and generous, and he had the bearing of a true gentleman.

sentences.zh: 協家雖貧素，而修飾邊幅，非車馬未嘗出遊。

translations.literal: Although Xie's family was poor and plain, he kept his appearance trim; unless there were carriage and horses he never went out on excursions.
translations.idiomatic: Although Xie's family was poor, he kept his appearance trim and never went out unless he had carriage and horses.

sentences.zh: 湘東王出鎮荊州，以為記室。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiangdong went out to govern Jing Province, he was appointed Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiangdong went out to govern Jing Province, Xie was appointed his Recorder.

sentences.zh: 時吳郡顧協亦在蕃邸，與協同名，才學相亞，府中稱為二協。

translations.literal: At the time Gu Xie of Wu Commandery was also in the prince's establishment; he shared the name Xie and his talent and learning were nearly equal, and in the establishment they were called the Two Xies.
