translations.idiomatic: At the time Gu Xie of Wu Commandery was also in the prince's establishment; he shared the name Xie and was nearly equal in talent and learning, so the staff called them the Two Xies.

sentences.zh: 舅陳郡謝暕卒，協以有鞠養恩，居喪如伯叔禮，議者甚重焉。

translations.literal: His uncle Xie Yan of Chen Commandery died; Xie, because of the debt of nurturing kindness, observed mourning as for an uncle, and commentators greatly respected this.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncle Xie Yan of Chen Commandery died, Xie observed mourning as for an uncle in gratitude for having raised him, and commentators greatly respected this.

sentences.zh: 又感家門事義，不求顯達，恒辭徵辟，游於蕃府而已。

translations.literal: He also, moved by his family's record of righteous service, did not seek prominence, constantly declined summonses and appointments, and merely moved within the prince's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his family's record of righteous service, he sought no prominence, repeatedly declined official summons, and contented himself with serving in the prince's establishment.

sentences.zh: 卒，元帝甚嘆惜之，為懷舊詩以傷之。

translations.literal: When he died, Emperor Yuan deeply lamented him and composed a poem recalling old times to mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Emperor Yuan deeply lamented his loss and composed a poem of remembrance to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 協所撰晉仙傳五篇，日月災異圖兩卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Xie's writings included Biographies of Jin Immortals in five chapters and Illustrations of Solar and Lunar Disasters and Omens in two scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Biographies of Jin Immortals in five chapters and Illustrations of Solar and Lunar Disasters and Omens in two scrolls, both of which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 其文集二十卷，遇火湮滅。

translations.literal: His collected writings in twenty scrolls were destroyed when they met with fire.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings in twenty scrolls were lost in a fire.

sentences.zh: 子之儀、之推，並早知名。

translations.literal: His sons Zhiyi and Zhitui both became famous early.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhiyi and Zhitui both won renown while still young.

sentences.zh: 紀少瑜字幼瑒，丹陽秣陵人也。

translations.literal: Ji Shaoyu, styled Youchang, was a native of Moling in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Shaoyu, style name Youchang, came from Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 本姓吳，養于紀氏，因而命族。

translations.literal: His original surname was Wu; he was raised by the Ji clan, and therefore took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Born a Wu, he was raised by the Ji family and took their name.

sentences.zh: 早孤，幼有志節，常慕王安期之為人。

translations.literal: He lost his father early; from youth he had purpose and integrity, and often admired the character of Wang Anqi.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he held fast to purpose and integrity from boyhood and often looked to Wang Anqi as a model.

sentences.zh: 年十三，能屬文。

translations.literal: At age thirteen, he could compose literary works.
translations.idiomatic: By thirteen he could already write polished prose.

sentences.zh: 初為京華樂，王僧孺見而賞之，曰：「此子才藻新拔，方有高名。

translations.literal: At first he wrote Jinghua music-poems; Wang Senru saw them and praised him, saying: "This boy's literary talent is fresh and outstanding; he will soon gain great renown.
translations.idiomatic: His earliest compositions were Jinghua music-poems. Wang Senru read them and was impressed. "This boy's talent is fresh and striking," he said; "he will soon be widely known.

sentences.zh: 」少瑜嘗夢陸倕以一束青鏤管筆授之，云：「我以此筆猶可用，卿自擇其善者。

translations.literal: " Shaoyu once dreamed that Lu Chui gave him a bundle of green inlaid brush-pens, saying: "These brushes of mine can still serve; choose the best among them for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: " Shaoyu once dreamed that Lu Chui handed him a bundle of green inlaid brush-pens, saying, "These brushes of mine can still serve—take whichever you find best.

sentences.zh: 」其文因此遒進。

translations.literal: " From that time his writing grew correspondingly vigorous and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: " From that time his writing grew markedly stronger.

sentences.zh: 年十九，始遊太學，備探六經，博士東海鮑皦雅相欽悅。

translations.literal: At nineteen he first entered the Imperial Academy, thoroughly exploring the Six Classics; the Erudite Bao Hao of Donghai deeply admired and delighted in him.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he entered the Imperial Academy for the first time and studied the Six Classics in full; the erudite Bao Hao of Donghai came to admire him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時皦有疾，請少瑜代講。

translations.literal: When Bao fell ill, he asked Shaoyu to lecture in his place.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao fell ill, he asked Shaoyu to lecture for him.

sentences.zh: 少瑜既妙玄言，善談吐，辯捷如流。

translations.literal: Shaoyu was skilled in abstruse discourse, eloquent in speech, and swift and fluent in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyu was masterful in abstruse discourse, fluent in speech, and quick as a stream in debate.

sentences.zh: 為晉安國中尉，即梁簡文也，深被恩遇。

translations.literal: He served as Chief Commandant of the Jin'an Principality, who was none other than the future Emperor Jianwen of Liang, by whom he was deeply favored.
translations.idiomatic: He served under the Chief Commandant of Jin'an—none other than the future Emperor Jianwen of Liang—and was deeply favored.

sentences.zh: 後侍宣城王讀。

translations.literal: Later he attended the Prince of Xuancheng in his studies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attended the Prince of Xuancheng as a reading companion.

sentences.zh: 當陽公為郢州，以為功曹參軍，轉輕車限內記室，坐事免。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Dangyang was governor of Ying Province, he appointed him Army Commandant Assessor; he was later transferred to Registrar within the Light Chariot General's staff, but was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Dangyang governed Ying Province, he made Shaoyu an army commandant assessor, then transferred him to registrar on the Light Chariot General's staff; he was later dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 大同七年，始引為東宮學士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong, he was first appointed a scholar of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Datong he was first made an Eastern Palace scholar.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王在郢，啟求學士，武帝以少瑜充行。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shaoling was at Ying, he memorialized requesting a scholar; Emperor Wu assigned Shaoyu to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shaoling was stationed at Ying, he petitioned for a scholar, and Emperor Wu sent Shaoyu to serve.

sentences.zh: 少瑜美容貌，工草書，吏部尚書到溉嘗曰：「此人有大才而無貴仕。

translations.literal: Shaoyu had a handsome appearance and was skilled in cursive script; Dao Gai, Minister of the Civil Service, once said: "This man has great talent but no lofty office.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyu was handsome and skilled in cursive script. Dao Gai, Minister of the Civil Service, once said, "This man has great talent but no high office.

sentences.zh: 」將拔之，會溉去職。

translations.literal: " He was about to promote him when Dao happened to leave his post.
translations.idiomatic: " He was about to promote him when Dao left his post.

sentences.zh: 後除武陵王記室參軍，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Registrar Assessor to the Prince of Wuling, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made registrar assessor to the Prince of Wuling and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 杜之偉字子大，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Du Zhiwei, styled Zida, was a native of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhiwei, style name Zida, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世儒學，以三禮專門。

translations.literal: His family had for generations pursued Confucian learning, specializing in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His family had for generations pursued Confucian learning, with a specialty in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 父規，梁奉朝請。

translations.literal: His father Gui served as Attendant at Court of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui had served as a court attendant under Liang.

sentences.zh: 之偉幼精敏，有逸才。

translations.literal: Zhiwei in youth was keen and clever, with outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zhiwei was quick and sharp, with gifts beyond his years.

sentences.zh: 年十五，遍觀文史及儀禮故事，時輩稱其早成。

translations.literal: At fifteen he had read widely in literature, history, and ritual precedents; contemporaries praised him as precocious.
translations.idiomatic: By fifteen he had read widely in literature, history, and ritual precedent, and contemporaries called him precocious.

sentences.zh: 僕射徐勉嘗見其文，重其有筆力。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xu Mian once saw his writings and valued their force of expression.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Mian once read his work and admired its force.

sentences.zh: 中大通元年，梁武帝幸同泰寺捨身，敕勉撰儀注。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited Tongtai Temple to offer his person in devotion to the Buddha, and ordered Xu Mian to draft the ritual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongdatong, Emperor Wu of Liang went to Tongtai Temple to yield his person in the Buddhist rite and ordered Xu Mian to draft the ceremonial protocol.

sentences.zh: 勉以先無此禮，召之偉草具其儀。

translations.literal: Xu Mian, noting there was no prior precedent for this rite, summoned Zhiwei to draft the full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Mian replied that the court had no precedent for it and summoned Zhiwei to sketch the full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 乃啟補東宮學士，與學士劉陟等抄撰群書，各為題目，所撰富教、政道二篇，皆之偉為序。

translations.literal: He was then recommended and appointed Eastern Palace Scholar; together with Liu Zhi and other scholars he copied and compiled various books, each with their own assigned topic; of the two treatises "Abundant Instruction" and "The Way of Governance," Zhiwei wrote both prefaces.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recommended as an Eastern Palace scholar and, with Liu Zhi and others, copied and compiled various books, each assigned its own topic; Zhiwei wrote the prefaces to both treatises he drafted, "Abundant Instruction" and "The Way of Governance."

sentences.zh: 後兼太學限內博士。

translations.literal: Later he also served concurrently as Erudite within the Imperial Academy establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He later also served concurrently as an erudite within the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 大同七年，梁皇太子釋奠于國學，時樂府無孔子、顏子登歌詞，令之偉制文，伶人傳習，以為故事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong, the Crown Prince of Liang performed the draping sacrifice at the National Academy; as the Music Bureau had no ascending hymn texts for Confucius and Yan Hui, Zhiwei was ordered to compose them; musicians learned and performed them, and they became established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Datong the Liang crown prince offered the Confucian libation at the national academy. The Music Bureau then lacked ascending hymns for Confucius and Yan Hui, so Zhiwei was ordered to compose them; the performers learned and kept them, and they became custom.

sentences.zh: 再遷安前邵陵王刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: He was twice promoted to Prison Assessor under the Prince of Shaoling, who was then stationed at Anqian.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to prison assessor under the Prince of Shaoling at Anqian.

sentences.zh: 之偉年位甚卑，特以強識俊才，頗有名當世。

translations.literal: Zhiwei's age and rank were quite low, yet by virtue of his powerful memory and outstanding talent he was quite renowned in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei was still young and low in rank, yet his powerful memory and outstanding gifts had already made him a name in his day.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書張纘深知之，以為廊廟之器。

translations.literal: Zhang Zuan, Minister of the Civil Service, knew him well and considered him material for the halls of state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan, Minister of the Civil Service, knew him well and regarded him as a future pillar of the court.

sentences.zh: 陳武帝為丞相，素聞其名，召補記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Chen Wudi was Grand Chancellor, having long heard of his name, he summoned him and appointed him Registrar Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Wudi was grand chancellor, having long heard his name, he summoned him and appointed him registrar assessor.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎，領大著作。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently served as Director of the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the secretariat and concurrently headed the historiography office.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，除鴻臚卿，餘並如故。

translations.literal: When Chen accepted the abdication, Zhiwei was appointed Director of Ceremonial; his other posts remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen accepted the abdication, Zhiwei was made director of ceremonial affairs; his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 之偉求解著作，優敕不許。

translations.literal: Zhiwei requested to be relieved of the historiography office, but an imperial edict graciously refused.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei asked to be relieved of the historiography office, but a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 再遷太中大夫，仍敕撰梁史，卒官。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Grand Master of Palace Affairs and was still ordered to compile the History of Liang; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to grand master of palace affairs and was still ordered to compile the History of Liang; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 文集十七卷。

translations.literal: His collected writings comprised seventeen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to seventeen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 顏晃字元明，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Yan Huang, styled Yuanming, was a native of Linyi in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Huang, style name Yuanming, came from Linyi in Langya.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，好學，有辭采。

translations.literal: He was orphaned and poor in youth, loved learning, and had literary grace.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he loved learning and had a gift for language.

sentences.zh: 解褐梁邵陵王兼記室參軍。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he became Concurrent Registrar Assessor to the Prince of Shaoling of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as concurrent registrar assessor to the Prince of Shaoling of Liang.

sentences.zh: 時東宮學士庾信使府中，王使晃接對，信輕其少，曰：「此府兼記室幾人？

translations.literal: At that time Yan Xin, an Eastern Palace scholar, was an envoy at the prince's headquarters; the prince had Huang receive and parry with him. Xin looked down on him for his youth and said: "How many concurrent registrars does this headquarters have?
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Palace scholar Yu Xin was sent to the prince's headquarters, the prince had Huang receive him. Xin, thinking him too young, asked, "How many concurrent registrars does this establishment have, anyway?

sentences.zh: 」晃曰：「猶當少於宮中學士。

translations.literal: " Huang replied: "It should still be fewer than the palace scholars.
translations.idiomatic: " Huang replied, "Still fewer than the palace scholars, I should think.

sentences.zh: 」當時以為善對。

translations.literal: " At the time this was considered a clever rejoinder.
translations.idiomatic: " Contemporaries judged it a sharp reply.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，奔荊州。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Hou Jing, he fled to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 承聖初，除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chengsheng era, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chengsheng era he was made vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉初，累遷員外散騎常侍，兼中書舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era of Chen, he rose through successive promotions to Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Concurrent Secretariat Steward, in charge of imperial edicts and proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chen's Tiancheng era he rose through successive promotions to supernumerary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and concurrent secretariat steward, in charge of edicts and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司農卿，諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted the title Director of the Directorate of Agriculture; his posthumous name was Zhenzi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made director of the directorate of agriculture, with the posthumous name Zhenzi, "The Upright."

sentences.zh: 晃家世單門，傍無戚援，而介然修立，為當世所知。

translations.literal: Huang came from a solitary household with no relatives for support, yet he stood apart in self-cultivation and was known to his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Huang came from a solitary household with no kin to lean on, yet he held himself upright in isolation and was known to his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 其表奏詔誥，下筆立成，便得事理。

translations.literal: His memorials, submissions, edicts, and proclamations flowed from his brush as he wrote, immediately capturing the substance of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials, submissions, edicts, and proclamations came from his brush at once and immediately hit the substance of the matter.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection of twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 岑之敬字思禮，南陽棘陽人也。

translations.literal: Cen Zhijing, styled Sili, was a native of Jiyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cen Zhijing, style name Sili, came from Jiyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 父善紆，梁世以經學聞，官至吳甯令，司義郎。

translations.literal: His father Shanyu was renowned for classical learning in the Liang era, rising to Magistrate of Wuning and Attendant for Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shanyu was known in the Liang for classical learning and rose to magistrate of Wuning and attendant for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 之敬年五歲，讀孝經，每燒香正坐，親戚咸加歎異。

translations.literal: When Zhijing was five, he read the Classic of Filial Piety; each time he burned incense and sat upright, and his relatives all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At five Zhijing read the Classic of Filial Piety; each time he burned incense and sat upright, and his kin all marveled.

sentences.zh: 十六，策春秋左氏、制旨孝經義，擢為高第。

translations.literal: At sixteen he was examined on the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Emperor's Exposition of the Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety, and was selected for the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he was examined on the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the emperor's exposition of the Classic of Filial Piety and was placed in the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 御史奏曰：「皇朝多士，例止明經，若顏、閔之流，乃應高第。

translations.literal: The Imperial Censor memorialized: "Our dynasty has many scholars who ordinarily pass only the Classics examination; only men of the caliber of Yan Yuan and Min Ziqian should receive the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial censor memorialized: "Our dynasty has many scholars who ordinarily pass only the classics examination; only men of the caliber of Yan Yuan and Min Ziqian should receive the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 」梁武帝省其策，曰：「何妨我復有顏、閔邪。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu of Liang reviewed his examination papers and said: "Why should I not have my own Yan Yuan and Min Ziqian?
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu of Liang reviewed his papers and said, "Why should I not have my own Yan Yuan and Min Ziqian?

sentences.zh: 」因召入面試。

translations.literal: " He therefore summoned him for a face-to-face examination.
translations.idiomatic: " He then summoned him for a face-to-face test.

sentences.zh: 令之敬升講坐，敕中書舍人朱異執孝經，唱士孝章，武帝親自論難。

translations.literal: He had Zhijing ascend the lecture seat, ordered Secretariat Steward Zhu Yi to hold the Classic of Filial Piety and recite the chapter "Filial Piety of the Scholar," and personally engaged him in disputation.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhijing ascend the lecture seat, ordered secretariat steward Zhu Yi to hold the Classic of Filial Piety and intone the chapter on the scholar's filial piety, and debated him himself.

sentences.zh: 之敬剖釋從橫，左右莫不嗟服。

translations.literal: Zhijing parsed and explained with sweeping mastery; none present failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing analyzed and explained freely in every direction; none present failed to admire him.

sentences.zh: 仍除童子奉車郎，賞賜優厚。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Gentleman Attendant of Carriages for the Youth Examination, with generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately made gentleman attendant of carriages for the youth examination, with generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 十八，預重雲殿法會，時武帝親行香，熟視之敬曰：「未幾見兮，突而弁兮。

translations.literal: At eighteen he attended a Buddhist assembly at Chongyun Hall; as Emperor Wu was personally offering incense, he gazed intently at Zhijing and said: "Not long since I saw you, and suddenly you wear the cap.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he attended the dharma assembly at Chongyun Hall; Emperor Wu personally performed the incense rite, gazed long at Zhijing, and said, "It seems but yesterday I saw you, and suddenly you wear the cap!

sentences.zh: 」即日除太學限內博士。

translations.literal: " That same day he was appointed Erudite within the Imperial Academy establishment.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he was made an erudite within the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 尋為壽光學士、司義郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he became a Scholar of Shouguang and Attendant for Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became a scholar of Shouguang and attendant for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，表請試吏，除南沙令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing, he petitioned to be tested as an official and was appointed Magistrate of Nansha.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing he petitioned to be tested as an official and was made magistrate of Nansha.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，除晉安王宣惠府中記室參軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng, he was appointed Registrar Assessor in the staff of Prince Xuanhui of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chengsheng he was made registrar assessor on the staff of Prince Xuanhui of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 時蕭勃據嶺表，敕之敬宣旨慰喻。

translations.literal: When Xiao Bo held the Lingnan region, Zhijing was ordered to proclaim the imperial will and offer reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Bo held Lingnan, Zhijing was ordered to proclaim the imperial will and reassure him.

sentences.zh: 會魏克江陵，仍留廣州。

translations.literal: When Wei captured Jiangling, he remained in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei captured Jiangling he stayed on in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳太建初還朝，授東宮義省學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taijian era of Chen he returned to court and was appointed Scholar of the Eastern Palace Righteousness Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chen's Taijian era he returned to court and was made a scholar of the Eastern Palace Righteousness Bureau.

sentences.zh: 累遷南台書侍御史，征南府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He rose through successive promotions to Secretariat Attendant Censor of the Southern Secretariat and Advisory Assessor of the Southern Campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to secretariat attendant censor of the Southern Secretariat and advisory assessor of the southern campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 之敬始以經業進，而博涉文史，雅有詞筆，不為醇儒。

translations.literal: Zhijing had first advanced through classical studies, yet he read widely in literature and history and possessed fine literary skill, and was not a narrow ritual scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing had entered through classical studies but ranged widely in literature and history, wrote well, and was no narrow ritual scholar.

sentences.zh: 性謙謹，未嘗以才學矜物，接引後進，恂恂如也。

translations.literal: By nature he was modest and careful; he never flaunted his talent and learning before others, and in guiding younger scholars he was ever gentle and courteous.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was modest and careful; he never flaunted his talent before others, and in guiding younger scholars he was ever gentle and courteous.

sentences.zh: 每母忌日營齋，必躬自灑掃，涕泣終日，士君子以篤行稱之。

translations.literal: On each anniversary of his mother's death he would hold a Buddhist fast, always sweeping the grounds himself and weeping all day; men of honor praised him for his devoted conduct.
translations.idiomatic: On each anniversary of his mother's death he held a Buddhist fast, always sweeping the grounds himself and weeping all day; men of honor praised him for his devoted conduct.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eleventh year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: A collection of ten scrolls by him circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of ten scrolls by him circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子德潤，有父風，位中軍吳興王記室。

translations.literal: His son Derun inherited his father's character and served as Registrar to the Prince of Wuxing of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Derun inherited his father's character and served as registrar to the Prince of Wuxing of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 何之元，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: He Zhiyuan was a native of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhiyuan came from Qian in Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 祖僧達，齊南台書侍御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengda was Secretariat Attendant Censor of the Southern Secretariat under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengda had been secretariat attendant censor of the Southern Secretariat under Qi.

sentences.zh: 父法勝，以行業聞。

translations.literal: His father Fasheng was known for upright conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fasheng was known for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 之元幼好學，有才思，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan loved learning from childhood and had literary gifts; when in mourning he exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan loved learning from childhood and had literary gifts; in mourning he went beyond what the rites required.

sentences.zh: 梁天監末，司空袁昂表薦之，因得召見。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Tianjian era of Liang, Minister of Works Yuan Ang recommended him in a memorial, and he was summoned to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Liang's Tianjian era, Minister of Works Yuan Ang recommended him in a memorial, and he was summoned to an audience.

sentences.zh: 累遷信義令。

translations.literal: He rose through successive promotions to Magistrate of Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to magistrate of Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 其宗人敬容，位望隆重，頻相顧訪，之元終不造焉。

translations.literal: His clansman Jingrong held weighty rank and prestige and frequently sought him out, but Zhiyuan never visited him in return.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Jingrong held weighty rank and prestige and often sought him out, but Zhiyuan never visited him in return.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，之元曰：「昔楚人得寵於觀起，有馬者皆亡。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Zhiyuan said: "In olden days a man of Chu won favor through Guan Qi, and those who had horses all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Zhiyuan said, "Long ago a man of Chu won favor through Guan Qi, and everyone who had horses perished.

sentences.zh: 夫德薄任隆，必近覆敗，吾恐不獲其利而招其禍。

translations.literal: When virtue is thin yet responsibility is heavy, ruin is near; I fear I would gain no profit but invite disaster instead.
translations.idiomatic: When virtue is thin yet responsibility is heavy, ruin is near; I fear I would gain no profit but invite disaster instead.

sentences.zh: 」識者以是稱之。

translations.literal: " Those who understood praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who understood praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，武陵王以太尉承制，授南梁州刺史、北巴西太守。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Hou Jing, the Prince of Wuling, exercising authority as Grand Marshal, appointed him Governor of Southern Liang Province and Administrator of Northern Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion the Prince of Wuling, exercising authority as grand marshal, appointed him governor of Southern Liang Province and administrator of Northern Baxi.

sentences.zh: 武陵王自成都舉兵東下，之元與蜀中人庶抗表請無行，王以為沮眾，囚之元於艦中。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wuling raised troops from Chengdu and marched east, Zhiyuan joined with the people of Shu in jointly memorializing against the campaign; the prince deemed this demoralizing the troops and imprisoned Zhiyuan aboard his warship.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling raised troops from Chengdu and marched east, Zhiyuan joined the people of Shu in jointly memorializing against the campaign; the prince deemed this demoralizing and imprisoned Zhiyuan aboard his warship.

sentences.zh: 及武陵兵敗，之元從邵陵太守劉棻之郡。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wuling's army was defeated, Zhiyuan followed Liu Fen, Administrator of Shaoling, to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling's army was defeated, Zhiyuan followed Liu Fen, administrator of Shaoling, to his commandery.

sentences.zh: 俄而魏克江陵，劉棻卒，王琳召為記室參軍。

translations.literal: Before long Wei captured Jiangling; Liu Fen died, and Wang Lin summoned him as Registrar Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wei captured Jiangling; Liu Fen died, and Wang Lin summoned him as registrar assessor.

sentences.zh: 及琳立蕭莊，署為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Lin enthroned Xiao Zhuang, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin enthroned Xiao Zhuang, he was appointed vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王琳敗，齊主以為揚州別駕，所居即壽春也。

translations.literal: When Wang Lin was defeated, the ruler of Qi appointed him Vice Administrator of Yang Province; his residence was at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lin was defeated, the ruler of Qi made him vice administrator of Yang Province; his residence was at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 及眾軍北伐，湘州刺史始興王叔陵遣功曹史柳咸齎書召之。

translations.literal: When the allied armies marched north, Prince Shixing Wang Shuling, Governor of Xiang Province, sent Clerk of Merit Liu Xian with a letter summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies marched north, Prince Shixing Wang Shuling, governor of Xiang Province, sent clerk of merit Liu Xian with a letter summoning him.

sentences.zh: 之元始與陳朝有隙，書至大惶恐。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan had previously had a falling-out with the Chen court; when the letter arrived he was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan had previously had a falling-out with the Chen court; when the letter arrived he was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 讀書至「孔璋無罪，左車見用」，遂隨咸至湘州。

translations.literal: When he read as far as the line "Chen Lin was guiltless, and Zuo Si was put to use," he followed Xian to Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When he read as far as the line, "Chen Lin was guiltless, and Zuo Si was put to use," he followed Xian to Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 再遷中衛府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Advisory Assessor of the Central Guard headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to advisory assessor of the Central Guard headquarters.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，移居常州之晉陵縣。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he moved to Jinling County in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he moved to Jinling County in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十三年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kaihuang of Sui he died at home.

sentences.zh: 徐伯陽字隱忍，東海人也。

translations.literal: Xu Boyang, styled Yinren, was a native of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Boyang, style name Yinren, came from Donghai.

sentences.zh: 父僧權，梁東宮通事舍人，領秘書，以善書知名。

translations.literal: His father Sengquan was Attendant Master of Affairs of the Eastern Palace under Liang and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, renowned for skill in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengquan served as Attendant Master of Affairs of the Eastern Palace under Liang and concurrently as Director of the Secretariat, and was renowned for his calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 伯陽敏而好學，善色養。

translations.literal: Boyang was quick-witted and loved learning, skilled in pleasing his parents in their presence.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang was quick-witted and loved learning, and excelled at caring for his parents with filial grace.

sentences.zh: 家有史書，所讀者近三千餘卷。

translations.literal: His household possessed historical works; what he had read amounted to nearly three thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His household possessed historical works, and he had read nearly three thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 梁大同中，為候官令，甚得人和。

translations.literal: In Datong of Liang he was Magistrate of Houguan and won great harmony among the people.
translations.idiomatic: During Datong under Liang he served as Magistrate of Houguan and won great harmony among the people.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，至廣州依蕭勃。

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Hou Jing he went to Guangzhou and attached himself to Xiao Bo.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellion of Hou Jing he went to Guangzhou and placed himself under Xiao Bo's protection.

sentences.zh: 勃平，還都。

translations.literal: When Bo was pacified, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo was pacified, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉中，除司空侯安都府記室參軍。

translations.literal: In Tianjia of Chen he was appointed Army Major and Master of Records in the household of the Minister of Works, Hou Andu.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianjia under Chen he was appointed Army Major and Master of Records in the household of Minister of Works Hou Andu.

sentences.zh: 太建初，與中記室李爽、記室張正見、左戶郎賀徹、學士阮卓、黃門郎蕭詮、三公郎王由禮、處士馬樞、記室祖孫登、比部郎賀循、長史劉刪等為文會友，後有蔡凝、劉助、陳暄、孔範亦預焉，皆一時士也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he formed a literary fellowship with Central Master of Records Li Shuang, Master of Records Zhang Zhengjian, Gentleman of the Left Household He Che, Scholar Ruan Zhuo, Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Xiao Quan, Gentleman of the Three Dukes Wang Youli, Recluse Ma Shu, Master of Records Zu Sun Deng, Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue for Comparisons He Xun, Chief Clerk Liu Shan, and others; later Cai Ning, Liu Zhu, Chen Xuan, and Kong Fan also joined—all were leading men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taijian he formed a literary fellowship with Li Shuang, Zhang Zhengjian, He Che, Ruan Zhuo, Xiao Quan, Wang Youli, Ma Shu, Zu Sun Deng, He Xun, Liu Shan, and others; later Cai Ning, Liu Zhu, Chen Xuan, and Kong Fan joined as well—all were leading literary men of the day.

sentences.zh: 游宴賦詩，動成卷軸。

translations.literal: At their gatherings and banquets they composed poetry, often filling whole scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: At their gatherings and banquets they composed poetry, often enough to fill whole scrolls.

sentences.zh: 伯陽為其集序，盛傳於世。

translations.literal: Boyang wrote a preface to their collected works, which circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang wrote a preface to their collected works, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 後除鎮北新安王府中記室參軍，兼南徐州別駕，帶東海郡丞。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Central Army Major and Master of Records in the household of the Prince of Xin'an, Defender of the North, and served concurrently as Vice Governor of Southern Xuzhou, with concurrent duty as Assistant Administrator of Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Central Army Major and Master of Records in the household of the Prince of Xin'an, Defender of the North, and served concurrently as Vice Governor of Southern Xuzhou with concurrent duty as Assistant Administrator of Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王為江州刺史，伯陽常奉使造焉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Poyang was Governor of Jiangzhou, Boyang was often sent on missions to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Poyang served as Governor of Jiangzhou, Boyang was often sent on missions to visit him.

sentences.zh: 王率府僚與伯陽登匡嶺置宴，酒酣，命筆賦劇韻三十，伯陽與祖孫登前成，王賜以奴婢雜物。

translations.literal: The prince led his staff and Boyang up Mount Kuang to hold a banquet; when the wine was warm he ordered brush and paper and assigned thirty difficult rhymes for composition. Boyang and Zu Sun Deng finished first and the prince rewarded them with servants and various goods.
translations.idiomatic: The prince led his staff and Boyang up Mount Kuang for a banquet; when the wine was flowing he ordered brush and paper and assigned thirty difficult rhymes. Boyang and Zu Sun Deng finished first, and the prince rewarded them with servants and various goods.

sentences.zh: 後除鎮右新安王府諮議參軍事。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Advisory Army Major in the household of the Prince of Xin'an, Defender of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Advisory Army Major in the household of the Prince of Xin'an, Defender of the Right.

sentences.zh: 聞姊喪，發疾卒。

translations.literal: On hearing of his elder sister's death he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of his elder sister's death he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 張正見字見賾，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhengjian, styled Jianze, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhengjian, styled Jianze, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖善之，魏散騎常侍、勃海長樂二郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shanzhi was Regular Attendant of the Cavalry in Wei and Administrator of the two commanderies of Bohai and Changle.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shanzhi served as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry in Wei and as Administrator of the commanderies of Bohai and Changle.

sentences.zh: 父修禮，魏散騎侍郎，歸梁，仍拜本職，遷懷方太守。

translations.literal: His father Xiuli was Vice Director of the Cavalry in Wei; he submitted to Liang and was again appointed to his former post, then promoted to Administrator of Huaifang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiuli served as Vice Director of the Cavalry in Wei; he submitted to Liang and was reappointed to his former post, then promoted to Administrator of Huaifang.

sentences.zh: 阮卓，陳留尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Zhuo was a native of Weishi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Zhuo was a native of Weishi in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖詮，梁散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan was Vice Director of the Cavalry under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan served as Vice Director of the Cavalry under Liang.

sentences.zh: 父問道，梁岳陽王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Wendao was Army Major and Master of Records in the household of the Prince of Yueyang under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wendao served as Army Major and Master of Records in the household of the Prince of Yueyang under Liang.

sentences.zh: 卓幼聰敏，篤志經籍，尤工五言。

translations.literal: Zhuo from youth was clever and keen, devoted to the classics, and especially skilled in five-word verse.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhuo was clever and keen, devoted to the classics, and especially skilled in five-word verse.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，父隨岳陽王出鎮江州，卒，卓時年十五，自都奔赴，水漿不入口者累日。

translations.literal: By nature he was deeply filial; his father followed the Prince of Yueyang to his posting in Jiangzhou and died there. Zhuo was then fifteen and rushed from the capital to the scene; for many days he took neither water nor food.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was deeply filial. His father had followed the Prince of Yueyang to his posting in Jiangzhou and died there; Zhuo was then fifteen and rushed from the capital. For many days he took neither water nor food.

sentences.zh: 載柩還都，度彭蠡湖，中流遇疾風，船幾沒者數四，卓仰天悲號，俄而風息，人以為孝感之至。

translations.literal: He bore the coffin back to the capital and crossed Lake Poyang; mid-lake they met fierce winds and the boat nearly sank several times. Zhuo looked heavenward and wailed; presently the wind ceased, and people took this as the utmost reach of filial response.
translations.idiomatic: He bore the coffin back to the capital and crossed Lake Poyang; mid-lake they met fierce winds and the boat nearly sank several times. Zhuo looked heavenward and wailed; presently the wind ceased, and people regarded this as the utmost power of filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 還除南海王府諮議參軍，以目疾不之官。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Advisory Army Major in the household of the Prince of Nanhai but, because of eye disease, did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Advisory Army Major in the household of the Prince of Nanhai, but because of eye disease he did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 退居裏舍，改構亭宇，修山池卉木，招致賓友，以文酒自娛。

translations.literal: He retired to his home village, rebuilt pavilions and halls, tended mountain pools and flowering trees, gathered guests and friends, and amused himself with literature and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to his home village, rebuilt pavilions and halls, tended mountain pools and flowering trees, gathered guests and friends, and amused himself with literature and wine.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，行至江州，追感其父所終，遘疾卒。

translations.literal: When Chen fell and he entered Sui, traveling as far as Jiangzhou he was overcome by remembrance of where his father had died, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell and he entered Sui, he traveled as far as Jiangzhou; overcome by remembrance of where his father had died, he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：文章者，蓋情性之風標，神明之律呂也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Literature is the banner of one's inner nature and the pitch-pipe of the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Literature is the banner of one's inner nature and the pitch-pipe of the spirit.

sentences.zh: 蘊思含豪，遊心內運，放言落紙，氣韻天成。

translations.literal: Thoughts stored and boldness held within, the mind roams in inner motion; words released onto paper, and breath and resonance are born of heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughts stored and boldness held within, the mind roams in inner motion; words released onto paper, and breath and resonance are born of heaven.

sentences.zh: 莫不稟以生靈，遷乎愛嗜，機見殊門，賞悟紛雜，感召無象，變化不窮。

translations.literal: All receive it from living spirit and shift with love and appetite; openings of insight have different gates, appreciation and understanding are tangled and mixed, stimulus and response have no fixed image, and transformation is inexhaustible.
translations.idiomatic: All receive it from living spirit and shift with love and appetite; openings of insight have different gates, appreciation and understanding are tangled and mixed, stimulus and response have no fixed form, and transformation is inexhaustible.

sentences.zh: 發五聲之音響，而出言異句，寫萬物之情狀，而下筆殊形。

translations.literal: It releases the sounds of the five tones yet produces words in differing lines; it depicts the conditions of the ten thousand things yet sets the brush to differing forms.
translations.idiomatic: It releases the sounds of the five tones yet produces words in differing lines; it depicts the conditions of the ten thousand things yet sets the brush to differing forms.

sentences.zh: 暢自心靈，而宣之簡素，輪扁之言，未或能盡。

translations.literal: What flows from the inner heart and is declared in plain simplicity—even the words of Wheelwright Bian could not fully exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: What flows from the inner heart and is declared in plain simplicity—even the words of Wheelwright Bian could not fully exhaust it.

sentences.zh: 然縱假之天性，終資好習，是以古之賢哲，咸所用心。

translations.literal: Yet though one may borrow from innate nature, in the end one relies on fond practice; therefore the sages of old all devoted themselves to it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though one may borrow from innate nature, in the end one relies on devoted practice; therefore the sages of old all devoted themselves to it.

sentences.zh: 至若丘靈鞠等，或克荷門業，或夙懷慕尚，雖位有窮通，而名不可滅。

translations.literal: As for men such as Qiu Lingju, some were able to bear the family vocation, others from early on cherished admiration and pursuit; though office had its limits of success and failure, their names cannot be extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: As for men such as Qiu Lingju, some were able to bear the family vocation, others from early on cherished literary ambition; though office had its limits of success and failure, their names cannot be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 然則立身之道，可無務乎。

translations.literal: Thus the way of establishing oneself—can one afford not to devote oneself to it?
translations.idiomatic: Thus the way of establishing oneself in the world—can one afford not to devote oneself to it?
